title: Best USB-C and Thunderbolt cables for iPhone, iPad and Mac for 2026
content:
Macworld





USB-C is the modern connection standard shared by most new devices today. It comes in several different formats—USB-C, USB4 and Thunderbolt—but they all have the same reversible connector at the end and are interchangeable and backwards compatible. All of Apple’s new devices now use USB-C or Thunderbolt for charging and data transfers.
Some cables are only really good for charging as their data-transfer (bandwidth) rate is too slow to be practical. In the reviews below we note both charging power (measured in watts) and data-transfer rate—measured in either megabits per second (Mbps) or gigabits per second (Gbps). If you are connecting the cable to a monitor, storage device, hub or docking station the minimum data speed should be 5Gbps but go higher if you can. If you just want to use it for charging an iPhone, iPad or MacBook, the data speed matters less.
We’ve tried and tested the best USB-C and Thunderbolt cables here. If you want to jump straight to our recommendations click the one that meets your requirements:
Best USB-C cable for iPhone and iPad
Best USB-C cable for Mac
Best Thunderbolt 5 cables
Best Thunderbolt 4 cables
You can find cheaper online but we recommend cables only from trusted brands, such as Anker, Apple, Beats, Belkin, Cable Matters, CalDigit, Native Union, Plugable, and Ugreen. When charging your precious devices, you want to be sure that you aren’t putting them at risk of overheating and potentially causing a fire in your home.
Apple’s old Lightning connector was also reversible—where it doesn’t matter which side of the connector faces up or down as you plug it in—so no big change there, but USB-C is much more than just a symmetrical design. It can transfer data much faster—pushing Lightning’s 0.48Gbps to up to 120Gbps.
Apple’s iPhone 15 and newer have a USB-C port, replacing the old trusty but proprietary Lightning cable that has been a part of iPhones and older iPads since 2012. Apple supplies a USB-C charging cable in the box, but if you want a single cable for fast charging and data transfers—or just a spare charging cable—we’ve rounded up some of our favorites to help you get the best one.
Some are fast, some are super-powerful, some are both, a few are retractable, and some are just fun. Yes… fun!
We go into more detail about everything you need to know about USB-C cables after the chart of best cables, but for now you need to know about the cable of your dreams:
Which speed (measured in watts) your devices require: an iPhone needs at least 20W to fast-charge, an iPad 30W, a MacBook Air at least 70W, a MacBook Pro 100W and the 16-inch Pro 140W. While the MacBook Neo doesn’t officially support fast charging, a 30W charger will speed things up but any higher won’t likely do much more for that laptop model.
Do you need it to transfer data as well as supply power? Most charging cables are limited to a rather slow 480Mbps data rate. If you want proper bandwidth as well as charging power look for at least 5Gbps or as much as 80Gbps.
How long should it be: if the charger is within arms reach of your device a short cable might suffice where a long cable will just be an inconvenience, but if you want to charge your iPhone, Pad or MacBook while sat on the sofa a longer cable will make all the difference.
We’ve supplied the cable data to these questions in our reviews below.
The difference between USB-A, Lightning and USB-C 

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Note that the cables reviewed here are USB-C to USB-C (or backwards-compatible Thunderbolt to Thunderbolt). Old iPhone chargers had the non-reversible rectangular USB-A connector to connect to the charger and a Lightning connector that went into the iPhone. Don’t stick with legacy USB-A at one end as the old standard is limited in data transfer speed to 10Gbps and limited in charging speed to just a rather pathetic 15W.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Using a USB-C charger will enable fast charging even for iPhones with a Lightning port. You can still charge an Apple device with a USB-A charger but not at the fastest speed. From the iPhone 15 onwards it’s USB-C into the charger and USB-C into the iPhone. See our roundup of the best USB-C chargers for iPhone.
We have even more tips that show you the fastest ways to charge an iPhone.
Best USB-C cables for iPhone and iPad
Elsewhere we have rounded up the best Lightning cables we’ve seen for iPhones older than the iPhone 15. USB-A is the larger, non-reversible connector. USB-C is required for iPhone fast charging.
From the iPhone 15 onwards—also with the AirPods Pro 2—you’ll need a cable with USB-C on both ends (USB-C-to-USB-C) to charge an iPhone or iPad unless you charge wirelessly: check out the best MagSafe wireless iPhone chargers.
All iPads on sale today feature a USB-C connector. But even the 10th Gen iPad’s USB-C is still limited to a 480Mbps data speed. The iPad mini has a USB-C port that supports 5Gbps; the iPad Air 10Gbps; and the iPad Pro has a USB4/Thunderbolt port that can zip data along at 40Gbps. Check your iPad’s data transfer rate before choosing a new cable.
For charging only, any of the USB-C cables reviewed below will be fine as 20W should be enough to charge even an iPad. But if you are connecting to other devices or syncing via cable, we recommend cables that support faster data transfers. A 10Gbps USB-C cable, such as the Cable Matters cord below, is an excellent option if you don’t want to spend a bundle on Thunderbolt.

Thunderbolt  cables
Macs use the Thunderbolt standard that is faster and more capable than USB-C. If all you require the cable for is charging, then the relevant USB-C charging cable should be fine, but for anything requiring fast data transfers go for higher-bandwidth Thunderbolt.
Standard copper “passive” Thunderbolt cables are also usually shorter as the data loses speed over longer distances. To get around this requires an “active” Thunderbolt cable that includes sophisticated chip engineering to push the signal along at the best speed, but you’ll see the price increase accordingly. Anything over 1m in length usually requires active technology.
Best Thunderbolt 5 cables
Thunderbolt 5 is superior to Thunderbolt 4 with doubled data/video bandwidth (80/120Gbps vs 40Gbps), improved PCIe 4.0 support (32Gbps vs 64Gbps), and enhanced power delivery (240W vs 100W). It’s backwards compatible all the way back to USB-C so—if you can afford it—it’s a more future-proof solution than Thunderbolt 3 or 4. Thunderbolt 5 transmits up to 80Gbps bidirectionally and 120Gbps in one direction with Bandwidth Boost enabled to support demanding display configurations.

Know your cables
Not all USB-C cables offer the same capabilities, so we explain each factor you need to consider. Fear not, for basic iPhone charging most USB-C cables will be fine. But some are finer than others. Macs use Thunderbolt cables that have the same Type-C connector as USB-C so look the same but have faster data transfer and charging speed options. You can use a Thunderbolt cable to charge USB-C devices, too.
Apple ships a USB-C Charge Cable with the newest iPhones but Mac users need to buy a Thunderbolt cable to connect to a docking station or fast storage device. Having a spare cable or two hanging around the house or office is always advisable—and there are better, cheaper, and more colorful USB-C and Thunderbolt cables than just those sold by Apple.
We’ve focused on USB-C charging cables as most people need them just to attach to a USB-C charger, but cables offer both charging and data transfers, although at different capabilities, depending on your requirements. 
Charging: All USB-C cables can carry a minimum of 60W (3A x 20V). Some support 100W (5A x 20V) charging, and some new Thunderbolt cables can charge at up to 240W. 60W is more than you need for a phone and is fine for the MacBook Neo and Air and 13-inch MacBook Pro. Go for at least a 100W cable for the 14-inch MacBook Pro. As Apple states 70W as the minimum for fast-charging the MacBook Air, a 100W cable is also recommended for these users. While 100W is fine for a 16-inch MacBook Pro, that model can be charged at up to 140W, although Apple restricts fast-charging for that model to its own $49/£49 USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable, which is included with all MacBooks.
iPhone 15-16 series: Apple says that the iPhone 15-16 can be fast-charged from zero to 50% in 30 minutes using at least a 20W USB-C power adapter, which is the same speed the iPhone 14 got via Lightning. Tests have shown that such iPhones can reach charging speeds of up to 30W so we think a 20W charger isn’t going to offer iPhone charging as fast as you can get. 
iPhone 17 series: Up to 50% charge in 20 minutes with 40W adapter or higher paired with USB‑C charging cable, and up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with 30W adapter or higher paired with MagSafe Charger.
iPhone 18 series: Up to a 50% charge in around 15 minutes when using 60W‑capable adapter or higher with Adjustable Voltage Supply paired with USB‑C charging cable, and up to 50% charge in 30 minutes with 35W adapter or higher paired with MagSafe Charger.
Check out our reviews of the best iPhone chargers.
Length: A long cable can be messy when your device is close to the charger, but a short one could leave your iPhone dangling out of reach. You may need different lengths of USB-C cable for each of your charging spaces. When it comes to transferring data, choose a cable that’s as short as you need as the longer the cable, the greater the risk of signal degradation—invest in a Thunderbolt 4 or 5 cable for 2m data-strength confidence. Or look at a coiled cable such as the Native Union POP Cable reviewed above.
Data transfer speed: iPhones with Lightning ports are limited to a slow USB 2.0 data transfer rate of just 480Mbps (480 megabits per second). Compare that to your Mac, whose Thunderbolt connection can reach up to 40Gbps on Thunderbolt 4 and 120Gbps on Thunderbolt 5—that’s 250 times faster! Data transfer speed doesn’t matter if all you are doing is charging a device but it is vital when connecting your Apple device to storage drives, docking stations, or monitors.
While the entry-level iPad is also limited to 480Mbps, the iPad Pro, like a MacBook, supports Thunderbolt’s 40Gbps maximum. The iPhone 15/16/17 and 15/16 Plus features USB-C that is limited to 480Mbps as with Lightning, but the iPhone 15/16/17/18 Pro and Pro Max’s USB-C can sync at 10Gbps—useful for backing up video or photos to a computer.
Note that the USB-C cable Apple supplies with the iPhone 15-18 families is a “Charge” cable and limited to 480Mbps for syncing. If you use the Pro or Pro Max model with a cable for data transfer, you’ll do better with a 10Gbps or higher bandwidth cable.





 FAQ 


1.
Which USB-C cable do I need to connect to a USB-C monitor
DisplayPort Alternate Mode is a feature available to USB-C and Thunderbolt that handles video as if the USB-C cable was a DisplayPort cable. USB-C monitors can therefore connect directly to your laptop or via a USB-C hub or USB-C or Thunderbolt dock.
However, not every USB-C cable supports video transfer so you need to choose the right type of cable.
If your external display supports a direct USB-C connection, look for a cable that has at least a data-transfer rate of 5Gbps for 4K at 60Hz or 10Gbps for 6K. For 8K we recommend you use at least a 40Gbps Thunderbolt 4 or USB4 cable or 80/120Gbps Thunderbolt 5 cable. The higher the bandwidth, the less risk of signal degradation.
Consider cable length, too. While compression technologies should kick in, the longer your cable, the more the signal can degrade so opt for as short a cable as you require when connecting from your MacBook or dock to a USB-C monitor. A fully featured C-to-C cable that is 1 meter or shorter will work just fine for 95% of what people need. The Cable Matters 10Gbps/100W 1m USB-C Cable is a recommended solution.
If you need a longer cable, a 2m Thunderbolt 4 or 5 cable, such as the Cable Matters 2m Thunderbolt 4 cable. See the reviews above for more options.
Some USB-C monitors can provide between 65W to 90W of passthrough power back to the laptop, so ensure your USB-C cable supports at least 100W if you want to use your USB-C monitor to power your laptop.





2.
Can you convert a Lightning cable to USB-C?
Apple has released a Lightning–to–USB-C adapter—confusingly named the Apple USB-C to Lightning Adapter ($29 at Apple’s U.S. store or £29 at Apple’s UK store) so you can convert an old Lightning cable into a USB-C cable for your new iPhone 15 or later, but, as you might expect from Apple, it’s way more expensive than just buying one of the new and superior USB-C cables we’ve reviewed above.





3.
What is the difference between Active and Passive Thunderbolt cables?
An “active” Thunderbolt cable contains built-in electronic chips that boost and repeat the data signal, allowing it to maintain stable, error-free full-speed (40Gbps) signals over longer distances compared to shorter “passive” cables that lack these chips.

content:

Cons

Our Verdict 
The Mac Studio’s SSD speed improvement is so dramatic that even if you bought an M4 Max or M3 Ultra Mac Studio–the previous models–you should consider upgrading to the M5 Max Mac Studio. Plus, the external display support is expanded. Sure it’s expensive, but if you want the best Mac ever made, accept no substitute.

With the M5 Max Mac Studio, there’s good news, and there’s great news. The good news is that it offers faster CPU processing and graphics. It’s a marginal boost over the previous generation, but faster is always good. The great news is that the improved SSD speed that was introduced with the M5 MacBook Pro comes to Apple’s top Mac.
The faster SSD is such a big deal that if you’re in a production environment and you invested in an M4 Max or M3 Ultra Mac Studio, you should seriously consider upgrading, even if the prices are higher. Time is money, and an investment in the current Mac Studio will be money well spent. Here’s our in-depth review of the M5 Max Mac Studio.
M5 Max Mac Studio: Our model’s specifications
The Mac Studio is available in two standard configurations: A $2,499 model with an M5 Max chip (18-core CPU, 32-core GPU) and 36GB of RAM, and a $5,499 model with an M5 Ultra chip with 96GB of RAM. Customers can customize their purchase by adjusting the number of CPU and GPU cores, and add more memory and SSD storage.

This review focuses on the M5 Max Mac Studio with a chip upgrade, additional RAM, and a larger SSD. Here are the specs of our review unit:
CPU: M5 Max with 18 cores (6 super cores, 12 performance cores), 16-core Neural Engine
GPU: 40 cores
Memory: 128GB unified memory (614GBps memory bandwidth)
Storage: 4TB SSD
Ports: 4 Thunderbolt 5/USB-C; 10Gb ethernet; 2 USB-A (USB 3); HDMI 2.1; 3.5mm audio; 2 USB-C; SDXC Card slot
Networking: Wi‑Fi 7 (802.11be); Bluetooth 6; Threads; 10Gb ethernet
Weight: 6 pounds (2.7 kg)
Dimensions: 3.7 x 7.7 x 7.7 inches (9.5 x 19.7 x 19.7 cm)
Price (as tested): $6,899/£6,899/CA$10,099/AU$10,899




				
					

				
			
The Mac Studio design reamins unchanged from its introduction in 2022.

Fundry




M5 Max Mac Studio: Performance
The odd M4 Max and M3 Ultra offerings Apple had with the previous Mac Studio were due to Apple skipping a generation with its Ultra chips. This time around, Apple decided that the M5 series would have an Ultra chip, so you can get either an M5 Max or M5 Ultra.
The $2,499 M5 Max Mac Studio comes standard with an 18-core CPU (6 super cores, 12 performance cores), a 32-core GPU, 36GB of unified memory, and a 512GB SSD. However, this CPU is essentially fixed at 36GB of RAM; if you want more, you must upgrade to the 18-core CPU/40-core GPU, which technically costs $300 but actually adds $600 to the price when the cost of the 48GB RAM upgrade is factored in. It can further be upgraded to 64GB ($400) or 128GB ($2,000).
This review looks at the M5 Max option with an 18-core CPU, a 40-core GPU, 128GB of RAM, and a 4TB SSD, which adds $4,400 the price of the Mac Studio. More about the pricing at the end of this review.


Blackmagic Disk Tests

Foundry






Typically, we start our reviews by looking at overall performance with Geekbench, and then we work our way through more specific aspects. But the SSD performance is so overwhelmingly good, it’s the story here. I mean, this chart doesn’t look correct, does it? Apple improved SSD performance with the M5 chip series, and we’ve seen big improvements in the M5 MacBook Pro. It’s finally come to the Mac Studio–it’s almost a shame that we had to wait so long. This is one of the key reasons why you should upgrade from another Mac Studio, even if you bought one this year. It’s a difference you’ll definitely feel.

Geekbench 7

Results are expressed as Geekbench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.

Foundry


Geekbench 7 was released just this year; it’s a general-purpose benchmark tool for gauging performance. The previous-generation M3 Ultra is faster than the M5 Max in multi-core CPU testing, but only by 9 percent. The difference between the M5 Max and the M4 Max that it replaces is more substantial at 22 percent.
The M5 Max’s Single-core CPU results are 8 percent faster than those of the M4 Max. We’ve seen improvements of 8 to 10 percent from generation to generation, so that result remains consistent.

Geekbench 6

Results are expressed as Geekbench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.

Foundry


Since Geekbench 7 is pretty new, we tested with Geekbench 6 for reference. Here, the M5 Max beats the M3 Ultra, but the margin is only 7 percent in the Multi-core tests–a difference you may not notice.

Cinebench 2026

Results are expressed as Cinebench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.

Foundry


Maxon also has a benchmark tool that tests more strenuously than Geekbench. Unfortunately, we don’t have data from older Mac Studios, so the results here are presented with the M5 Pro Mac mini and the M5 MacBook Pro. Still, you can get a sense of how much and improvement you can experience if you move up the chip series.

Cinebench 2024

Results are expressed as Cinebench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.

Foundry


We do have Cinebench 2024 results from the previous Mac Studio lineup, and the M5 Max provides a 10 percent GPU boost over the M3 Ultra. The GPU improvement over the M4 Max is a more noticeable 33 percent.

Geekbench AI Neural Engine

Results are expressed as Geekbench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.

Foundry



Geekbench AI GPU

Results are expressed as Geekbench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.

Foundry


The Mac Studio has become extremely popular for AI development. Our benchmark records don’t go that far back with this test, so we’ve included other M5 chips for reference. The M5 Max’s Neural Engine offers a vast improvement over the M4 Max and the M3 Ultra–that a boon for AI developers.
One thing to consider with the Mac Studio and AI is the RAM configuration. To get more than 36GB of RAM, you need to upgrade from the base M4 Max chip, which bumps the price by at least $600, as I outlined earlier.

iMovie video export

Results are times in seconds. Lower times/shorter bars are faster.

Foundry


The speed gain that the M4 Max had over the M2 Max Mac Studio was much more significant than the one we see between the M4 Max and M5 Max. Keep in mind that the previous comparison actually skips a chip generation since Apple didn’t make an M3 Max Mac Studio.

Handbrake video encode

Results are times in seconds. Lower times/shorter bars are faster.

Foundry


Another test where the difference between the M4/M5 Max and M2 Max are drastic. The change is much more dramatic when you do not use hardware acceleration.


Geekbench 7 Compute

Results are expressed as Geekbench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.

Foundry






The M3 Ultra posts faster Metal scores in Geekbench 7’s Compute test, but it has a CPU with twice as many core (80 versus the M5 Max’s 40-cores).


Geekbench 6 Compute

Results are expressed as Geekbench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.

Foundry






With Geekbench 6, the M3 Ultra shows a more significant lead over the M5 Max, but again, it’s an 80-core GPU against a 40-core CPU.

Video game benchmarks

Results are frames per second. Higher rates/longer bars are faster.

Foundry


We saw frame rate boosts of 30 percent or more in Total War: Warhammer III and Borderlands 3. Our results with Civilization VI, an older game, were flat.
In all, the multi-core CPU improvements are a tad bit more than the typical increase of 15 percent (or so) that we’ve seen between generations, with the M5 Max showing a boost of 20 percent or more over the M4 Max in many of our tests. 
If the CPU performance isn’t enough to convince you to upgrade, then take a look at the GPU, where the M5 Max even outperforms the M3 Ultra. Combine that with the SSD improvement, and what we have is proof that Apple can continue to offer significant progress with its chips to make the cheaper Mac Studio a compelling machine atop the Mac lineup.
M5 Max Mac Studio: Thunderbolt 5 ports
Apple upgraded the Thunderbolt ports to Thunderbolt 5 with the previous Mac Studio, so those same ports are on the current model. The throughput is 80Gbps that can go up as high as 120Gbps, but you need a Thunderbolt 5 cable and a supported device to reach those top speeds.

				
					

				
			
Mac Studio rear ports.

Fundry




The M5 Max Mac Studio supports up to five displays, four over Thunderbolt at 6K/60Hz or 4K/165Hz, and one connected to the HDMI port at 5K/60Hz. The M5 Max Mac Studio also can drive three displays, with two displays at 8K/60Hz or 5K/120Hz or 4K/240Hz, and a third HDMI display at 5K/60Hz. These supported specs are improved over the M4 Max Mac Studio, so the new Mac Studio’s display support gets a boost.
M5 Max Mac Studio: Same ol’ good stuff
This iteration of the Mac Studio is a chip upgrade and nothing much else (besides the boosted display support, which is tied to the chip.)  The design is the same as it has been since the Mac Studio’s introduction in 2022, and it’s not likely to change for a long while. The port configuration is also the same, and the keyboard, mouse, and display are sold separately.
Speaking of display, Apple did release new displays earlier this year, though you might be able to find something comparable to Apple’s $1,499 Studio Display–it’s not a bad display, it’s just that it’s quite pricey. The Studio Display XDR is also expensive, but it’s the display that professionals who demand top-notch color and image quality will want.
M5 Max Mac Studio: Price
Except for its non-upgradeable design, there hasn’t been a “catch” with the Mac Studio until now. That catch is the higher price. The base M5 Max model starts at $2,499, a $500 increase over the M4 Max Mac Studio, but no more expensive that it was after Apple hiked prices in June. However, the Ultra Mac Studio went up in price again. In June, Apple increased the M3 Ultra Mac Studio’s starting price from $3,999 to $5,299, and now Apple has raised the starting price of the M5 Ultra another $200 to $5,499.

				
					

				
			
Apple increased the Mac Studio price last June, and made more price increases with this new release.

Foundry




These are steep increases, enough to make anyone pause, even if you’re using a model from the M2 generation. If you feel like you can’t ever get enough speed, then you won’t blink at the higher prices. Others might want to wait. But I think these higher prices aren’t going to go down, even if the supply chain shortages that cause them eventually get resolved. These prices are the new normal, so some Mac buyers will need to reset their personal upgrade cycles.
Should you buy the M5 Max Mac Studio?
If you’re a Mac Studio user, you need a fast Mac. Apple’s improvements to the SSD are so compelling that even if you have an M4 Max or M3 Ultra Mac Studio, you should consider upgrading. Yes, it’s a pricey proposition, but your workflow will notice the improvement. But if you have a older Mac Studio and working with AI, you could wait for the next generation, because future M-series chips promise to have better AI capabilities. In that case, waiting isn’t a bad idea.
However, like I said, the Mac Studio is a pricey proposition, and if you’re an individual professional whose means of offsetting the cost of purchase aren’t as immediate as, say, someone in a bigger production house, then continue to enjoy your current Mac Studio investment. If you’re new to the Mac Studio, I recommend buying a current model over an older M4 Max or M3 Ultra Mac Studio. The faster SSD is worth it alone.

title: iFixit Shares iPhone 18 Pro Teardown With Inside Look at New Features
content:
iFixit today published an iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max teardown in both article and video formats, providing a closer look inside the new devices.


The teardown confirms the battery capacities for the eSIM-only models:

iPhone 18 Pro: 4,288 mAh (+0.8% vs. 4,252 mAh for iPhone 17 Pro) 
iPhone 18 Pro Max: 5,567 mAh (+9.4% vs. 5,088 mAh for iPhone 17 Pro Max)
eSIM-only models of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are sold in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, and Kuwait. The devices have a SIM card tray in all other countries.

surfaced previously.

The teardown also provides an in-depth look at the new variable aperture system on both models, the larger vapor chamber for cooling, and more.



NAND now sits inside the dual-layer logic board, which makes storage-related repairs less convenient, according to iFixit. In addition, the screen's plastic frame cracked or broke away on three of the four iPhone 18 Pro models it opened, which is a new issue that it did not face with previous models. However, iFixit said further testing is needed.

title: Should you buy a Mac mini now? M6 vs M5 Pro buying advice
content:
Macworld





It’s a good time to buy a Mac mini. Apple announced the new M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini on August 25, with shipping from September 22. With another significant update unlikely soon, there is little reason to wait if you need a compact desktop Mac.
For most buyers, we recommend the M6 Mac mini. Starting at $899/£899 – up from $599 for the M4 generation – it offers improved performance for everyday work, coding and creative tasks. It is particularly appealing if you already own a monitor, keyboard and mouse, or are replacing an Intel Mac or early Apple silicon model.
The M5 Pro Mac mini is aimed at more demanding users. Its faster CPU and GPU, Thunderbolt 5, greater memory bandwidth and support for up to 64GB of unified memory make it better for professional creative work, development and larger local AI models. However, prices start at $1,699/£1,699 and rise quickly with upgrades.
This guide explains whether to buy now, which model to choose, how much to pay, and the alternatives, drawbacks and refurbished options to consider.


Should you buy a Mac mini now? 
There are reasons to wait. Discounts are likely to improve in the months after launch, particularly around Prime Day in October and Black Friday in November, and more refurbished or discounted M4 models may appear as buyers upgrade. If you’re happy with your current Mac, want to see independent benchmarks first or simply want the lowest possible price, there is no need to rush.
You may prefer not to risk waiting. A global memory shortage contributed to long delivery times and limited availability for the previous generation, and similar supply constraints could affect the new models. The higher cost of memory and other components has also contributed to the Mac mini’s substantial price increase.
Buy Mac mini now if:
You need a Mac mini now and want the latest model.
You’re replacing an Intel Mac or an older Apple silicon Mac.
You want a powerful compact desktop for everyday, office, development or creative work.
The $899/£899 M6 Mac mini provides all the performance you need.
Consider M5 Pro if:
You need more than 32GB of unified memory.
You run demanding professional creative or development workloads.
You want to run larger local AI or LLM workloads.
You need Thunderbolt 5 or substantially greater memory bandwidth.
Wait if: 
You want to see independent benchmarks of the new models.
You’re hoping for discounts around Prime Day or Black Friday.
Your current Mac still meets your needs.
You don’t need a new Mac urgently and want to see whether prices fall.
Consider refurbished if:
You can find an M4 Mac mini at a significant discount.
You want the best value rather than the newest chip.
An Apple-refurbished M4 or M4 Pro configuration meets your memory and storage needs.
You’re comfortable waiting for refurbished M6 or M5 Pro stock to appear.  


						

							




		
Apple Mac mini (M6, 2026)
$879.99 at Amazon										 | 
										$899 at Apple							
						
Apple Mac mini (M5 Pro, 2026)
$1,669.99 at Amazon										 | 
										$1699 at Apple							
						




						

							




Which Mac mini to buy: M6 or M5 Pro? 

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary / Foundry




The Mac mini lineup has changed significantly in 2026, with Apple introducing the M6 and M5 Pro models in August. The choice between them comes down to your workload and budget, as they serve very different audiences despite sharing the same compact design.
Apple sells two Mac mini models, both announced on August 25 and shipping from September 22, 2026:
Mac mini (M6) — starts at $899 / £899
12-core CPU, 12-core GPU
16GB unified memory (up to 32GB)
Up to 2TB SSD
Thunderbolt 4 (three ports), two front USB-C ports, HDMI, 2.5Gb Ethernet (10Gb Ethernet optional)
Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread
Supports up to three displays (two 6K + one 5K)
Mac mini (M5 Pro) — starts at $1,699 / £1,699
15-core CPU, 16-core GPU (upgradeable to 18-core CPU, 20-core GPU for +$200)
24GB unified memory (up to 64GB)
Up to 8TB SSD
Thunderbolt 5 (three ports), two front USB-C ports, HDMI, 2.5Gb Ethernet (10Gb Ethernet optional)
Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread 
Supports up to three 6K displays
Despite the “M5” name being a generation older than “M6,” the M5 Pro is the more powerful chip — it has more CPU and GPU cores, substantially greater memory bandwidth – 307GB/s, compared with 153GB/s or 170GB/s for the M6, depending on the memory configuration, and supports far more unified memory.
Choose the M6 Mac mini if:
You don’t need more than 32GB of unified memory (RAM).
You need a compact, powerful desktop for everyday use – web browsing, office work, photo editing, coding, and general productivity.
You’re a student or budget-conscious buyer looking for the best-value option for home offices, school or office use. Education pricing brings the starting price down to $799.
You already own a monitor, keyboard, and mouse.
You don’t need the extra performance or connectivity of the M5 Pro model.
Choose the M5 Pro Mac mini if:
You’re a developer, video editor, 3D artist, musician, or researcher who needs sustained performance for demanding workloads.
You want to run larger local AI models. The M5 Pro’s higher memory ceiling and much greater memory bandwidth make it better suited to heavier LLM workloads than the M6. If local AI is a priority, choose your memory carefully because it cannot be upgraded later.
You need Thunderbolt 5 for faster external storage, high-bandwidth peripherals or professional video workflows.
You regularly work with heavy 3D rendering, high-end video production, large codebases or scientific workloads.
You need more than 32GB of unified memory.






M6 Mac miniM5 Pro Mac mini

Best forEveryday work, coding and mainstream creative workSustained professional and AI workloads
Starting price$899/£899$1,699/£1,699
Memory16GB–32GB24GB–64GB
Memory bandwidth153GB/s or 170GB/s307GB/s
StorageUp to 2TBUp to 8TB
ThunderboltThunderbolt 4Thunderbolt 5
DisplaysTwo 6K plus one 5KThree 6K
Our verdictBest choice for most peopleBuy only if your workload requires it

 






How much should you pay for Mac mini?
M6 Mac mini, starting at $899. 
M5 Pro Mac mini, starting at $1,699. 
Since the August 2026 update, the Mac mini is no longer the budget Mac it once was. The M6 model starts at $899, $300 more than the $599 starting price of the M4 generation.
For most people, the $899 M6 Mac mini is the model to buy. It offers more than enough performance for everyday work, browsing, media and general productivity, although the standard 16GB of unified memory and 256GB SSD may feel limiting if you plan to keep it for several years.
If you need more demanding performance for creative work, development or running local AI models, the M5 Pro Mac mini starts at $1,699. Configurations with more memory and storage can quickly push the price towards $3,000, so it only makes sense if you genuinely need that extra performance.
Be cautious about spending heavily on Apple’s storage upgrades. External SSDs and Mac mini hubs with NVMe storage can provide considerably more capacity for less money.
For most buyers, we recommend spending around $899 on the M6 Mac mini. Move up to the M5 Pro only if you need its extra processing power or significantly more memory.
Discounts are likely to appear at Amazon and other resellers over time, particularly around Prime Day in October and Black Friday in November. For now, the best bargain may be a discounted M4 Mac mini, although remaining stock is likely to be limited.
Find Apple on Amazon U.S. 
Find Apple on Amazon U.K.
Students can save $100 through Apple’s Education Store, reducing the M6 Mac mini to $799 and the M5 Pro model to $1,599. Apple’s Refurbished Store is another way to save, although it may be some time before the new M6 and M5 Pro models appear there. Read: How to get an Apple student discount at Apple’s Education Store and Should you buy a refurbished Mac. 


						

							


Reasons to buy a Mac mini

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Excellent value: The price has gone up, but the Mac mini remains one of the most versatile and cost-effective ways to enter the macOS ecosystem. Even at the new starting price of $899, the Mac mini still delivers excellent performance per dollar. That balance of price, power, and efficiency is one of the main reasons for the desktop’s growing popularity. It also offers access to professional-grade performance for significantly less cash than a similarly specced MacBook Pro.
Long software support window: The M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini will have a long usable lifespan and will receive many years of macOS updates and security support. 
Compact desktop footprint: The Mac mini’s ultra-compact 5-inch square design makes it one of the most space-efficient desktop computers available. It fits easily under monitors, in small offices, or in minimalist workstation setups. Its compact form factor also makes it particularly attractive for server racks, home labs, and multi-machine deployments. 
Retail discounts and refurbished deals: Despite already offering strong value at full price, the Mac mini is occasionally discounted by third-party retailers. If you can find a Mac mini deal – even on a M4 model with a  higher-memory configuration – we recommend taking advantage of it. The Apple Refurbished Store can offer even better value, assuming stock is available. In the past, we have seen the M4 Mac mini discounted by around $100/£100, while M4 Pro models have dropped by approximately $200/£210. If deals like these reappear, they are likely worth considering.


						

							


Reasons not to buy Mac mini
The price has gone up significantly: The Mac mini was once the undisputed budget Mac, but that is much harder to say now. The entry-level model has risen sharply in price, making it less compelling for buyers primarily looking for the cheapest way into the Mac ecosystem. At $899, the latest Mac mini is still less expensive than a MacBook or iMac, but it no longer feels like the bargain it once was.
You need to buy your own peripherals: The Mac mini is a “BYODKM” – Bring Your Own Display, Keyboard and Mouse – computer. That’s central to its appeal if you already own those accessories, but it can add substantially to the cost if you don’t. Unlike an iMac or MacBook, the Mac mini doesn’t include a display, keyboard or mouse. Buying all three can easily add hundreds of dollars to the overall price. The latest models also lack USB-A ports, so you may need adapters or a hub if you still use older accessories.
It’s not portable: The Mac mini is a desktop computer, so it isn’t suitable if you need to work in different locations. You can’t easily take it to a lecture, meeting or coffee shop in the way you can a MacBook. For students, frequent travellers or anyone who regularly works away from a desk, a laptop is likely to be the better choice.
You can’t upgrade it later: You need to choose your memory and storage carefully when you buy because neither can be upgraded afterwards. Apple’s build-to-order memory and storage upgrades can also be expensive, particularly once you start moving beyond the base configuration. This can quickly push the Mac mini into MacBook Pro or Mac Studio territory. Storage is less of a concern because inexpensive external SSDs and Mac mini hubs with NVMe storage can add capacity later, but there is no equivalent workaround for unified memory.
Availability could be limited: New Mac launches can sometimes bring longer delivery times for popular configurations, particularly higher-memory or build-to-order models. The M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini may suffer significant shortages due to their popularity and the shortage of components and memory.
It’s not ideal for every AI workload: Apple is increasingly positioning its Macs for AI workloads, with the M6 GPU’s Neural Accelerators and dual 16-core Neural Engine, but as our colleagues at PCWorld explain, the Mac mini has some limitations if running large local models is your main priority. The standard M6 Mac mini tops out at 32GB of unified memory, which may be restrictive for particularly large local models. The M5 Pro model offers more memory, but higher-spec configurations become expensive quickly. There is also no support for Nvidia’s CUDA platform. Many professional AI and machine-learning tools are optimized around CUDA and Nvidia GPUs, so a Windows or Linux PC with a suitable Nvidia graphics card may be faster or better supported for some workloads. For general Apple Intelligence features and lighter local AI use, however, this shouldn’t be a concern.


						

							


What to avoid when buying a Mac mini

				
					

				
			
IDG




Intel: Avoid Intel-powered Mac mini models – when shopping for a refurbished Mac mini, prioritize models with Apple Silicon (M-series chips). 
Low RAM: We advise avoiding 8GB RAM models if possible, as newer generations now start with 16GB as the base standard. 
Check status: Check whether an older model is classified as vintage or obsolete. Service for vintage Macs depends on parts availability, while Apple generally ends hardware service for obsolete Macs. See: How long do Macs last.


						

							




Is Mac mini right for you?
Is the Mac mini the best choice for you? There are a number of trade-offs to consider. 


FeatureConsideration

PortabilityNot portable; requires separate monitor, keyboard, and mouse.
ConnectivityLacks USB-A ports; may require adapters for older accessories. The M5 Pro Mac mini features three Thunderbolt 5 ports, while the standard M6 model uses Thunderbolt 4. 
UpgradabilityUnified memory and internal storage cannot be upgraded by the user after purchase.

 



Who is the Mac mini best for?


UserRecommendation

Student, office work, web devBuy M6 Mac mini (or M4 if a refurbished model is available)
Creative work (photo/video)M6 for mainstream photo/video work; M5 Pro for sustained professional workloads
Local AI / LLM workloadsM5 Pro with as much unified memory as the workload requires
Existing M1/M2 Mac mini ownerConsider M6 if performance, display support, connectivity or memory limits justify upgrading
Intel Mac ownerBuy M6 Mac mini

 






Mac mini vs Mac Studio: Which should you buy?

				
					

				
			The Mac Studio is an even more powerful option.
Thomas Bergbold 




The choice between the Mac mini and the Mac Studio largely comes down to whether you prioritize value or maximum performance.
The Mac mini offers some of the best value in Apple’s desktop lineup. Even the standard M6 model delivers impressive performance for everyday computing, creative work, software development, and local AI tasks, while the M5 Pro configuration provides power for more demanding workloads.
The Mac Studio is designed for users who need workstation-class performance. Following the discontinuation of the Mac Pro, it is now effectively Apple’s most powerful desktop. Starting at $2,499/£2,499 for the M5 Max configuration, the Mac Studio also represents the most affordable way to get a Max-series Apple Silicon chip (which starts at $4,099/£4,099 if you buy a MacBook Pro). It is well suited to professional video production, large AI models, 3D rendering, and other heavily multi-threaded or GPU-intensive workflows.
For most users, the Mac mini is a better value purchase. However, if your workloads demand high performance, more memory and a more powerful GPU, the Mac Studio is the better choice. 


						

							


Mac mini vs MacBook Neo: Which is better value?

				
					

				
			
Thomas Armbrüster




Before the introduction of the MacBook Neo, the Mac mini was Apple’s least expensive Mac. That is no longer the case – particularly now Apple has raised the price of the entry-level Mac mini from $599/£599 to $899/£899.
The MacBook Neo is now Apple’s most affordable Mac, starting at $699/£699. It is designed as an entry-level Mac and is powered by the A18 Pro chip originally used for the iPhone 16 Pro and only offers 8GB memory. The focus is on portability, battery life, and affordability rather than performance.
The Mac mini, by contrast, remains Apple’s best-value desktop Mac for users who already own a monitor, keyboard, and mouse. Thanks to its M6 and M5 Pro chips, active cooling system, and greater performance, it is better suited to demanding workloads such as coding, creative applications, multitasking, and local AI development.


						

							


Where to buy a Mac mini 
If you’re looking to buy a Mac mini, you can choose between Apple, third-party retailers and refurbished outlets.
Apple: You can buy a Mac mini directly from the Apple Store online or at an Apple retail store. 
Apple Education Store: Apple also offers discounted education pricing for eligible students and educators via its Education Store. For example, the $899 M6 Mac mini costs $799 with education pricing.
Third-Party Resellers: It’s worth checking third-party retailers as well as Apple, as stores such as Amazon and B&H frequently discount Macs. Authorized resellers and major retailers often sell the Mac mini at less than Apple’s list price.
In the U.S., retailers include:
Amazon
Best Buy
B&H Photo Video
Costco
Adorama
DataVision
In the U.K., retailers include:
Amazon
Argos
Currys
John Lewis
AO
Ebuyer
Laptops Direct
The U.K. also has Apple Premium Resellers including KRCS, iStore, Select, Albion and Jigsaw.


						

							


Should you buy a refurbished Mac mini?
A refurbished Mac mini can be an excellent way to save money, particularly if you don’t need the latest model. Discounts can be significant, although the exact saving depends on the model, configuration and seller.
The best place to start is Apple’s Refurbished Store. Apple’s refurbished Macs are fully tested, cleaned and inspected, and come with a one-year limited warranty, 90 days of technical support and eligibility for AppleCare. They are also supplied with the appropriate accessories and repackaged in a new box.
Earlier in 2026, we saw refurbished M4 Mac mini models discounted by around $90/£90, with savings also available on the M4 Pro version. However, as of September 2026, refurbished Mac mini stock is very limited. M4 models are currently unavailable, and it may be some time before the new M6 and M5 Pro models start appearing in Apple’s refurbished store.
Availability is one of the main drawbacks of buying refurbished. Stock depends on returns and trade-ins, so you may not find the exact memory or storage configuration you want. More models may become available as owners upgrade to the latest Mac minis and older machines make their way to refurbishers.
You should also be careful when buying from third-party sellers. Refurbishment standards and warranties can vary, and marketplaces may contain much older Intel-based Mac minis. We generally wouldn’t recommend those models now unless the price is exceptionally low, as Apple silicon Mac minis offer much better performance and will receive software support for longer.
We’ve found Amazon particularly worth checking carefully. Refurbished stock can be dominated by Mac minis from 2020 or earlier, and we’ve even seen discontinued configurations listed for more than their original selling price. Always check the model year, specification and price of an equivalent new Mac before buying.
Buying refurbished is generally safer than buying second hand from a private seller. A reputable refurbished Mac should have been inspected and tested and will usually include a warranty and returns policy. A privately sold Mac may offer neither, and there is also a risk of Activation Lock if the previous owner hasn’t properly removed the Mac from their Apple Account.
Where to buy a refurbished Mac mini
U.S.: Amazon, Back Market, Best Buy, GainSaver, Mac of All Trades and Refurb.me.
U.K.: Affordable Mac, Amazon, Back Market, Hoxton Macs, MacFinder, Mac4Sale and MusicMagpie.
Read our guide to the pros and cons of buying refurbished Macs. We also have recommendations of the best places to buy a refurbished Mac.

title: Popping your iPhone 18 Pro into last year’s case? Not so fast
content:
Macworld





Apple’s latest iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max look identical to the previous iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max generation, with a few minor visual differences such as a smaller Dynamic Island at the front and, of course, the new colors (RIP Cosmic Orange). The brushed aluminum unibody chassis and camera plateau are practically identical, and according to Apple’s tech specs, they have the exact same measurements:
iPhone 17 Pro dimensions
Height: 5.91 inches (150mm)
Width: 2.83 inches (71.9mm)
Depth: 0.34 inches (8.75mm)
iPhone 18 Pro dimensions
Height: 5.91 inches (150mm)
Width: 2.83 inches (71.9mm)
Depth: 0.34 inches (8.75mm)
iPhone 17 Pro Max dimensions
Height: 6.43 inches (163.4mm)
Width: 3.07 inches (78mm)
Depth: 0.34 inches (8.75mm)
iPhone 18 Pro Max dimensions
Height: 6.43 inches (163.4mm)
Width: 3.07 inches (78mm)
Depth: 0.34 inches (8.75mm)
The iPhone 18 Pro is slightly heavier, weighing 211g versus the iPhone 17 Pro’s 204g; Pro Max 249g vs 233g, but that’s the result of what’s inside: the new A20 Pro chip, Apple cellular modems, and a new vapour chamber. So it would seem that any iPhone 17 Pro case would be compatible with the newest phones. That might not be the case (no pun intended).

				
					

				
			
TORRAS




Will an iPhone 18 Pro fit in a case for an iPhone 17 Pro?
Even though the 18 Pro and 17 Pro phones have the same dimensions, there’s a barely perceptible physical difference: The camera bump on the iPhone 18 Pro/Max is about 0.5mm taller than on the iPhone 17 Pro/Max. That’s not an iPhone 18 Pro measurement that Apple tracks in its tech specs.
So while you’d expect that the iPhone 18 Pro can fit in a case made for the iPhone 17 Pro, some might fit a little too snugly or look a little off, much like if you put an iPhone 16 Pro in an iPhone 17 Pro case (which also kind of works). It varies by brand and case type.
In the course of our testing of new cases for the iPhone 18 Pro series, we found numerous case makers that list 17 Pro/18 Pro compatibility. When we reached out for clarification, leading case manufacturer OtterBox told Macworld that its iPhone 18 Pro/Max cases are “also compatible with iPhone 17 Pro, so the cases can be used interchangeably between those two models.”
Similarly, Decoded told us that all its iPhone 18 cases “are also compatible with the iPhone 17 models.” Mous acknowledged that while “the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max lineup has a taller camera bump, our iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max cases will also fit” the 18, but noted that its new cases “are custom-built for each device to guarantee a perfect fit and protection”.
However, several case makers disagreed on the case compatibility between 17 and 18 iPhones. In particular, cases designed with tight tolerances might therefore have a problem with the 18’s taller camera bump.
For example, Rokform, which specializes in rugged cases, told Macworld that any iPhone 18 Pro case will be compatible with both iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro models. However, its older iPhone 17 Pro case lineup is not compatible with iPhone 18 models due to camera plateau design differences. 
Wave told Macworld that it developed its eco-friendly cases specifically for the 18 Pro & 18 Pro Max, with a slightly increased lip for camera protection.
So, the bottom line is this: You should be able to fit a 17 Pro/Max in a new case designed for the 18 Pro/Max, but the opposite might not be true. So if you’re shopping for a new case for your new iPhone 18 Pro, make sure you get one that specifcally says it’s compatible with the iPhone 18 Pro. 
New cases are custom-built for each device to guarantee a perfect fit and protection, so buying a case built specifically for your iPhone model is always the safest option: see our roundup of the best cases for iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max and best cases for iPhone 17.

title: Sorry Android, even the ‘dull’ iPhone is still the hottest handset around
content:
Macworld





This was expected to be a momentous year for the iPhone, and for once, reality lived up to the hype. The iPhone Duo is a wonder of engineering and industrial design, and offers hope that foldable phones can finally enter the mainstream. It’s fun, a little flawed, but totally different from everything Apple has done previously, and exactly what fans have been crying out for the company to do: take a risk.
Oh, and there’s also a new set of Pro-branded iPhones with minor iterative upgrades on the previous generation. Obviously nobody’s excited about them, right?
But if that’s the case, what was going on at Apple Stores last Friday? As the software designer Parker Ortolani reported on Twitter/X, both sides of the plaza at New York’s Fifth Avenue were packed that day as customers lined up for the new products. There were similar crowds reported at Covent Garden in London, Orchard Road in Singapore, Queen Street in Brisbane, and numerous other stores around the globe. Customers weren’t shopping for the Duo, to be clear, since you can’t even per-order it until October 16. Rather they were all in line for one of four products: AirPods 5 (implausible), Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4 (unlikely), or the main suspect: the iPhone 18 Pro.
Which is odd, because the 18 Pro is objectively quite a dull phone. For a start, it looks exactly the same as the 17 Pro, and only a few external tweaks separate it from even 2022’s iPhone 14 Pro. There are two new colors, but neither are anywhere near as vibrant as last year’s wildly popular Cosmic Orange (which, for reasons best known to Apple’s crack marketing team, has been killed off). It’s hard to believe customers are going mad for the 18 Pro’s looks.
The flagship new feature is a variable-aperture camera system, something I look forward to testing when I get my 18 Pro, but hardly something which will revolutionize the user experience for the average iPhone buyer. It’s been generations since iPhone Pro cameras were anything less than superb; last year a $60m movie was (mostly) shot on an iPhone 15 Pro Max. Photographic upgrades these days are doomed to be minor and applicable only to a niche group of users in a niche set of circumstances.
Beyond the colors and the cameras, what’s changed? It’s faster, obviously (not that you’ll notice the difference on the apps you’re using). The display is actually very slightly bigger, thanks to the shrinking of the Dynamic Island. The battery life is better, and it’ll charge quicker, too. These are all nice, sensible upgrades, but they’re not exactly thrilling. It’s solid evolution, as compared to the Duo’s revolution.
So why are people inconveniencing themselves around the world simply to be among the first to get hold of a decent but hardly groundbreaking phone? Rationally speaking, joining the line on launch day is a colossal waste of time and effort. Far better to buy in advance and get your new phone delivered to your house. Or wait a couple of weeks, check the reviews before committing to a purchase, and stroll into a half-empty shop at whatever time suits you.
Worse, everyone knows it’s a bad idea, and some of the most annoying people on the internet can’t wait to tell you. The comments on any video or news story covering the launch crowds inevitably fill up with professional parade-rainers rushing to point out that the iSheep are being taken for a ride once again, and what they should actually do is… well, probably buy an Android phone instead. But certainly never take joy in a silly consumer ritual promoted by the wrong corporation.
The naysayers aren’t entirely wrong. But humans aren’t always rational. And I find it oddly reassuring that even after 19 years, the iPhone still holds the power to trigger the same old irrationally human response. September comes round, Apple shows off the new iPhone, and fans flock to the stores to be with their people. New CEO John Ternus, who attended the iPhone 18 Pro’s launch in New York, will have been heartened to see that his company still has a community like no other tech company. It bodes well for his time in charge.

title: iPhone 20 Pro Display Sizes Leak Ahead of 2027 Launch
content:
Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone lineup could feature slightly larger displays than the iPhone 18 Pro models, if a new leak shared on Weibo is accurate.


Prolific Chinese leaker Digital Chat Station claims that early iPhone 20 Pro display specifications include a 6.41-inch screen with a resolution of approximately 2,686 × 1,236 pixels, while the iPhone 20 Pro Max is said to have a 6.96-inch display with a resolution of around 2,912 × 1,340 pixels.

For comparison, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max feature 6.27 inches (rounded to 6.3 inches) and 6.86 inches (rounded to 6.9 inches) respectively. Those figures are measured as a standard rectangle, while the actual viewable area is smaller because of the devices' rounded corners. Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max resolutions are 2,622 × 1,206 pixels and 2,868 × 1,320 pixels, respectively.

marketed as a 7-inch panel if it reaches production.

Apple last increased the size of its premium iPhone displays with the iPhone 16 Pro lineup in 2024. The iPhone 16 Pro grew from 6.1 to 6.3 inches, while the iPhone 16 Pro Max increased from 6.7 to 6.9 inches, thanks to slimmer bezels and slightly larger chassis dimensions. The leaked dimensions for the iPhone 20 Pro models suggest only a modest increase in overall screen size, but there could be a good reason for this. 

multiple reports indicating that Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone could resemble a single, uninterrupted slab of glass where the metal frame bezels are largely hidden during normal use. Bloomberg reported in June that Apple had started ramping up work on two sizes of the 20th anniversary iPhone.

thinner and brighter OLED panels for the devices, along with under-display Face ID and potentially an under-display front-facing camera. However, Digital Chat Station says Apple is now testing a smaller Dynamic Island-style hole-punch design for the iPhone 20 Pro models that sounds similar to the new iPhone 18 Pro models, suggesting Apple may still be testing multiple approaches. 

iPhone Duo offer a timely example of the kind of challenge that Apple is likely facing in its quest to create an uninterrupted display design. Unless it can improve the implementation, a cutout for the front camera may be the compromise Apple has to make for the iPhone 20 Pro models.

title: Siri AI Settlement Website Now Live: Apple to Pay Some iPhone Owners
content:
In May, Apple agreed to pay $250 million to settle a U.S. class action lawsuit over Siri AI's delayed launch, and the settlement website is now live.


Apple will pay an estimated $25 per eligible iPhone to eligible customers, who can submit a claim via the settlement website between September 21 and December 21 of this year. The exact payment may be higher or lower than $25 depending on the total number of valid claims submitted and other factors, with the maximum amount set at $95.

Apple denies all of the allegations made in the lawsuit. Apple agreed to the settlement to avoid the costs and risks of a trial.

Below, we have answered some key questions regarding the lawsuit.

Why Was Apple Sued?

In June 2024, Apple previewed new Siri capabilities powered by Apple Intelligence, including understanding of a user's personal context, on-screen awareness, and deeper per-app controls. For example, Apple showed an iPhone user asking Siri about their mother's flight and lunch reservation plans based on info from the Mail and Messages apps.

in a TV commercial starring actor Bella Ramsey, and elsewhere.

delayed the launch of the personalized version of Siri, leading to the company being hit with a class action lawsuit alleging false advertising.

In a statement, Apple touted a range of other Apple Intelligence features it had already released. Nevertheless, Apple agreed to settle the lawsuit "to stay focused" on "delivering the most innovative products and services to our users."

finally announced Siri AI at WWDC 2026 in June. Siri AI is available on iPhone 15 Pro models and newer running iOS 27, which was released last week.


Siri AI is still considered a beta feature even though iOS 27 is no longer in beta.

Am I Eligible?

To be eligible to submit a claim, you must reside in the U.S. and have purchased one of the iPhone models listed below in the U.S. for purposes other than resale between June 10, 2024 and March 29, 2025.


  
iPhone 15 Pro

  
iPhone 15 Pro Max

  
iPhone 16

  
iPhone 16e

  
iPhone 16 Plus

  
iPhone 16 Pro

  
iPhone 16 Pro Max

Over the coming days, eligible customers should be notified about the settlement in an email, which will contain a claim ID and a PIN code. But, the settlement website also offers an option to submit a claim without this information.

The claims form asks for your personal information and the eligible iPhone's serial number. If you indicate that you do not have the serial number, the form asks for your Apple Account email address and the eligible iPhone's phone number.

How Much Will Apple Pay Me?

According to the terms of the settlement, each person who files an eligible claim will receive a per-device payment of $25, but this amount could increase up to $95 if the total number of claims submitted is lower than anticipated.

Where and When Can I Submit a Claim?

You can submit a claim on the settlement website between September 21 and December 21.

When Will I Receive Payment?

A final approval hearing is scheduled for February 24, 2027, so payments to customers are not expected to begin until some point next year.

What Else Should I Know?

The settlement website answers some common questions about opting out of the settlement and other important topics, so be sure to read it carefully.

title: Top Stories: iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate Out Now, Siri AI Waitlist, and More
content:
All of Apple's products introduced at last week's event with the exception of the iPhone Duo are now available, with the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5 all launching on Friday.


While new hardware is always a welcome arrival, users of existing hardware also got big upgrades this week with the releases of iOS 27, macOS Golden Gate and more. Apple is also already looking ahead to iOS 27.1 that will ship with the iPhone Duo next month and iOS 27.2 that will see the first significant round of improvements to iOS 27 for all users, so read on below for all of details on these stories and more!

Top Stories

Apple Releases iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 With Siri AI and Liquid Glass Update

Following last week's big iPhone event, this week saw the traditional public release of Apple's new major operating system updates, headlined by iOS 27 and iPadOS 27.


iOS 27 brings new Siri AI capabilities to users in many countries around the world, as well as a variety of other new features and improvements. For a quick introduction to iOS 27, check out our list of 10 features to try first, and when you're ready for more, move on to our look at 50 new things your iPhone can do in iOS 27.

iOS 27 Ultimate Mega Guide links to all of the feature coverage we've been putting together for the release.

macOS Golden Gate Now Available With Siri AI, Visual Intelligence and More

On the Mac side, this week saw the release of macOS Golden Gate 27. The update introduces Siri AI, a smarter chatbot version of ‌Siri‌ with a dedicated ‌Siri‌ app. It also brings Visual Intelligence to the Mac for the first time, and tweaks the look of the Liquid Glass design update Apple introduced last year.


For a quick overview of what's new in macOS Golden Gate, be sure to check out our list of 10 features to try first, including Siri AI, easier creation of Shortcuts and Safari Extensions, performance improvements, and more, and then move on to our guide to 50 new features and changes for a more in-depth look.

Apple Says iPhone 18 Pro Max Sold in U.S. Differs in One Way

Following last week's introduction of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, there was some confusion over the cellular modems included in the devices, with it appearing that Apple's own C2 modem was only included in the iPhone 18 Pro.


Apple later updated its spec pages for the new models around the world, making it clear that the C2 is included in both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in every country around the world EXCEPT for the iPhone 18 Pro Max in the United States. That device continues to use the Qualcomm Snapdragon X80 modem from the iPhone 17 Pro models, but Apple has yet to explain the reason for this difference.

Reminder: iOS 27's All-New Siri AI Has a Waitlist, Here's How to Sign Up

If you recently installed iOS 27 on your iPhone, you might be wondering where the new-and-improved Siri AI and dedicated Siri app are. In case you missed it, you must join Apple's waitlist in order to gain access to these new features.


Keep in mind that while iOS 27 is compatible with the iPhone 11 and newer, Siri AI is limited to the iPhone 15 Pro and newer. It is also not currently available at all in EU countries due to Apple's regulatory battle with the European Commission over Digital Markets Act requirements.

For those who are eligible for Siri AI, joining the waitlist is a simple process in the Settings app. Once on the list, wait times seem to vary, with some users receiving access to Siri AI within a few minutes of signing up and others having to wait a few hours or even days.

Apple Releases First iOS 27.2 Beta

With iOS 27.0 out the door, Apple this week seeded the first beta of iOS 27.2 and related updates to developers for testing purposes. Yes, that's right...iOS 27.2, not 27.1.


The biggest change in the first iOS 27.2 beta is the revamped Health app that Apple showed off at last week's iPhone event, although Apple says it won't be included in the public release of the update, so the general public will need to wait a bit longer for it to be available. For more, check out our full list of everything new in the first beta of iOS 27.2.

iCloud+ Now Includes Apple TV, Apple Arcade, and Curated Apple Music Stations in Over 100 Countries

Apple this week announced a new subscription initiative that turns paid iCloud+ subscriptions into a broader services bundle in more than 100 countries.


In select countries, Apple says every paid iCloud+ plan, including the cheapest 50GB tier, now includes Apple TV and Apple Arcade "at no additional cost," while family sharing extends the storage, TV and Arcade access to up to five people.

title: Apple Exec Says 'Hold Us Accountable' on iPhone Duo Crease
content:
Apple hardware engineering VP Tom Marieb spoke with TechRadar and shared some candid thoughts about Apple's upcoming iPhone Duo.


The ‌iPhone Duo‌ uses a matte nano-texture display, which is meant to cut down on glare and minimize the visibility of the crease. When asked if the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s crease would be more visible over time, as that's what tends to happen on other foldables, Marieb said the nano-texture display would help. He asked people to hold the company "accountable" on crease visibility.
Hold us accountable to that, please. The choice of a matte finish — apart from it being beautiful — is part of that equation. When you look at glossy displays, their specularity makes it very easy to pick up topology differences. That's part of the reason we picked the matte finish — it's not only beautiful in terms of preventing glare, but it's also more forgiving of [hinge] changes over time.

Marieb said the ‌iPhone Duo‌'s hinge was something he was "especially proud of" because it took a long time to get the right design. Apple wanted a durable hinge that felt solid to open and close.
We really worked on the torque profile very heavily, and that means changing a lot of the mechanical properties of the hinge to have it feel solid, like a high-end automobile's car door, when you shut it. That was design intent, so people would have a feeling like, 'Oh, it's okay. This is well crafted, and it's safe for me to use and not worry about it.'

Apple didn't want the hinge to be "floppy," so torque had to be perfected for different use cases. The hinge Apple came up with lets the ‌iPhone Duo‌ be used in partially folded seated and standing modes, as well as open and closed. Marieb said "a lot of blood, sweat, and tears" went into the hinge design.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Max Requires 'Prepare to Ship' Battery Drain Before Shipping
content:
The iPhone 18 Pro Max has a battery capacity over 20 watt-hours, which means there are additional shipping requirements. If an ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max needs to be shipped somewhere, its maximum battery capacity has to be limited through firmware.


According to Apple, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max uses an "innovative battery-firmware solution" that limits battery capacity to below 20Wh between when the iPhone is manufactured and its delivery to a customer. Activating the iPhone removes the limit to make the battery's full charging capacity available. iPhones that are not yet activated or still in the box will not need Prepare to Ship because they are already limited to under 20Wh.

Customers who need to ship the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max for repair, trade-in, or other purposes have to use a new Prepare to Ship feature. Prepare to Ship discharges the battery to below 20Wh and sets a charge limit so the iPhone stays below the threshold during the shipping process.

The Prepare to Ship option can be accessed by going to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Prepare to Ship. Apple warns that the iPhone can become "warmer than usual" during Prepare to Ship if the battery needs to be discharged. When finished, the iPhone shows a "Ready to Ship" status in Settings.

If Prepare to Ship needs to be undone, there is an option in the same section of the Settings app to undo the shipping preparation. Depending on the reason the user selected for the Prepare to Ship feature, there could be a 14-day waiting period before it can be disabled.

title: Hands-On With the Apple Watch Series 12
content:
The Apple Watch Series 12 came out today, and we picked one up to get a look at the new feature set. There are no major external changes, but Apple updated the device's internals and health sensors.

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.

The Apple Watch Series 12 has the same design as the Series 11, but it does come in different colors. The aluminum models are available in a light gold shade that's distinct from the rose gold Apple used last year, as well as dark bronze, black, and space gray. There are also ceramic models in pearl white and night blue, and polished titanium models in radiant gold and natural. On the aluminum models, Apple is now using Ceramic Shield 2 instead of Ion-X glass, and the new material is 60 percent tougher.

You might not be able to tell a Series 11 apart from a Series 12 when looking at the front, but the back has been updated. Apple says the upgraded sensors make the Apple Watch Series 12 the most accurate wearable for heart rate sensing.

The Series 12 has a Health Sensing System that pairs the new sensors with an S11 chip that's faster than the S10 in the prior-generation model. It takes heart rate readings every five seconds now and measures heart rate variability as often as every five minutes.

It's early, but so far we haven't seen the higher sampling rates cause excessive battery drain. The Apple Watch Series 12 is still rated for all-day battery life, and charging is faster this year. You can get up to 12 hours of normal usage from a 15-minute charge, but you need to use the Apple Watch charger that comes with the Series 12. Older chargers won't give you the faster charging rate.

The Health Sensing System powers a readiness score that lets you know whether to go all-out on activity or take a rest day. It's based on metrics such as recent activity, vitals, and sleep, and will adjust as the day continues. It takes about a week of data collection from the Series 12 before you start getting a readiness score.

Live Rewind and Siri Recap features, but those won't be available until later this year.

Even though the Apple Watch hasn't seen a design refresh, the health features make this a decent update. You may not want to upgrade if you have the Series 10 or Series 11, but anything older is worth upgrading from.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 vs. Ultra 4 Buyer's Guide
content:
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 bring new health sensors, a new chip, and more detailed recovery insights to Apple's smartwatch lineup, so how do they compare?


Both models feature the S11 chip, 4GB of RAM, 64GB of storage, and the new Health Sensing System, which measures heart rate every five seconds throughout the day. They also share Readiness, Recovery HRV, daytime vitals, improved step tracking, hypertension notifications, sleep apnea notifications, Sleep Score, and more. This means that the Ultra 4's higher price does not buy you more advanced everyday health tracking.

Apple Watch Ultra 4 starts at $799. The gap narrows if you want a premium case material, with the titanium Series 12 starting at $699. This year, the Series 12 also gains a ceramic option starting at $899, making it more expensive than the Ultra despite its smaller size and shorter battery life.

The Apple Watch Ultra continues to focus on durability, extended battery life, and additional capabilities for activities like diving and exploration. Our guide helps to answer the question of how to decide which of these two Apple Watches is best for you. For most users, the Apple Watch Series 12 is the better choice. It offers the same performance, health sensors, Readiness insights, and Audio Intelligence features as the Ultra 4 in a thinner, lighter device. The aluminum model delivers these benefits for $400 less, making it the stronger option for everyday use and regular workouts.

The Ultra 4's most broadly useful advantage is battery life. Its longer endurance makes overnight wear and extended workouts easier to fit around charging. You do not need to be an endurance athlete to appreciate less frequent charging, but the premium is easier to justify if the Series 12 cannot comfortably cover your usual activities and charging habits.

For hiking away from cellular coverage, recreational scuba diving, or very long events, the Ultra has a clearer purpose. Satellite communications, dual-frequency GPS, greater water resistance, and extended workout modes address needs that the Series 12 cannot fully meet. The Action button and brighter display may also appeal to enthusiasts who simply want more capable hardware.

Size and appearance remain substantial trade-offs. The Ultra is considerably bulkier and heavier despite offering a display only slightly larger than the 46mm Series 12's. The Series 12 is more discreet and offers polished titanium and ceramic finishes, making it better suited to buyers who prioritize comfort or appearance. Try on the Ultra before buying if you are unsure about its size.

For this week's giveaway we've teamed up with iMazing to offer MacRumors readers a chance to win an iPhone Duo and a copy of the iMazing software to go along with it.


If you're unfamiliar with iMazing, it's Mac and PC software that offers a speedy, simple way to manage all of the data on your iPhone. You can make backups, add and delete photos, videos, and music, save content like messages, and much more.

While Apple has the built-in Finder on Mac for managing an iPhone, iMazing has a ton of features Apple doesn't offer. You can set up automatic backups with snapshots that make it easy to find what you're looking for and selective restore for bringing back just what you need. A useful search tool lets you find files on your devices and in your backups.


There's a Device Overview with detailed information about your iPhone in one spot, and dedicated tools for browsing, exporting, and archiving content. You can transfer photos, music, books, movies, and other media files from your computer to your iPhone and vice versa. You can even create an entire archive of your messages from the Messages app or WhatsApp.

iMazing can be used for screen recording on macOS, and there are diagnostic and device-info export tools. A Spyware Analyzer lets you know if any of your devices have been compromised.


The software isn't limited to the iPhone. It works with the iPad and Vision Pro, along with older devices like the iPod. If you have an old iPod with music on it, you can use iMazing to get it off. It also supports song transfers from non-iOS music players.

iMazing was entirely overhauled in 2024, and since then, the software has continued to get regular updates to add new features. The user interface has been updated with a collapsible sidebar and customizable device and backup list views, and data export has been improved. You can export all of your data with advanced filters, and use the same filters on the Unified Logs browser. Business features have improved too, with streamlined MDM enrollment, a Command Line Interface for advanced interaction with iOS devices and backups, and the iMazing Profile Editor 2 for configuring macOS app, notification, and login permissions.


You'll never have to worry about a device being unsupported with iMazing. It's updated with ongoing support for new models as they come out. In the near future, iMazing plans to add Android support, which will make it even more useful. iMazing can be downloaded from the iMazing website at prices starting at $30. iMazing has personal subscriptions, family subscriptions, and enterprise subscriptions, with free trials available. Some functions are free without a purchase.
