title: iPhone 18 Pro: Using the New Variable Aperture Lens
content:
Like the iPhone 17 Pro models, the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max have three rear cameras – a 48MP Fusion Main lens, an 8x48MP Telephoto lens, and a 48MP Ultra Wide lens. They also share the same focal lengths and resolutions as their predecessors. The big upgrade this year though is the new variable aperture on the Main camera. Let's dive in.


Aperture is what controls how much light enters the lens and hits the sensor. If too little light hits that sensor, images tend to be blurry and/or grainy. To compensate, the shutter has to stay open longer, or it has to turn on Night Mode. The problem with this approach is that the longer the shutter stays open or Night Mode is engaged, the more likely that the imagery will be blurry. Even still photos can lack sharpness and definition.

The solution is to use a variable aperture lens that is physically able to let more or less light in depending on the shot, which in turn allows for variations in shutter speed. The iPhone 18 Pro models can do this automatically, or you can take over the process manually for more stylistic control.

To achieve this, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max trade a fixed ƒ/1.78 aperture for a four-stop variable aperture ranging from ƒ/1.48 to ƒ/4.0, delivering around 50 percent better low-light performance and giving photographers optical control over depth of field that the iPhone has never offered before.


As mentioned, you can leave the iPhone 18 Pro to do its thing with the new variable aperture, or you can take control of it manually. Here's how it's done:

In the Camera app, tap the button with six dots at the bottom-right of the interface.

Select Lens Aperture from the control pane.

Tap one of the four circles to set the aperture: from left to right they range ƒ/1.48, ƒ1.8, ƒ2.8, and finally, ƒ/4.0.

If you change your mind, tap the Auto button on the left to let the iPhone automatically control the aperture.


Try experimenting with different aperture settings to see how they affect your images. The ƒ/1.48, for example, produces a more shallow depth of field, while the ƒ/4.0 will have more of the image in focus.

title: Apple Reportedly Accepts Even Higher RAM and Storage Prices in 2027
content:
Apple has agreed to pay Samsung even higher prices for RAM and storage chips starting in the first quarter of 2027, according to a DigiTimes report this week citing an earlier report from Chinese publication Jiemian News.


Apple has reportedly agreed to pay nearly $2 per Gb of DRAM and $0.33 per Gb of NAND storage. This is a 30% to 40% increase in pricing for these chips compared to what Apple is paying in the third quarter of 2026, according to DigiTimes.

It is unclear if this reported agreement will lead Apple to further raise prices on products like iPhones, iPads, and Macs, or if the company has already factored in the more expensive components in early 2027 into its current 2026 prices.

You may also be wondering which screen size suits you, how much storage you need, or whether to save money with an older model rather than buy the latest iPhone. You’ll also want to consider which model offers the best balance of features and value.
In this guide, we explain the differences between every iPhone currently available from Apple, paying particular attention to prices, cameras, displays, performance, battery life, durability and design. By the end, you should have a much clearer idea of which iPhone best meets your needs.
If you simply want to know which models we recommend, you can also read our full iPhone reviews, linked below, and use our iPhone comparison chart to compare the latest models with the other iPhones Apple sells.

How to choose an iPhone
To help you narrow down the right iPhone model, we’ll look at the key questions that matter most when choosing an iPhone, including which has the best camera, battery life, display and performance, how much storage you need, and which model offers the best value.


Which iPhone has the best camera? 

				
					

				
			
Apple




The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max have the best camera systems of any current iPhone. Both use the same triple-48MP rear camera setup, so there is no photographic advantage to choosing the larger Pro Max unless you also want its bigger display and longer battery life.
The headline upgrade is the 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, a first for the iPhone. You can switch between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8 and ƒ/4.0, giving you more direct control over depth of field and low-light shooting. The Pro models also add a 48MP Ultra Wide and 48MP Telephoto camera, with 4x native telephoto and an 8x optical-quality zoom option. Apple also provides manual controls for aperture, shutter speed, white balance and histogram viewing, plus ProRAW, ProRes RAW and Apple Log 2 support.
The iPhone 17 remains an excellent camera phone for most people. It has a 48MP Main camera and 48MP Ultra Wide camera, plus a 12MP optical-quality 2x option cropped from the Main sensor. It also gains the 18MP Center Stage front camera, which can automatically reframe shots and supports Dual Capture. What you miss compared with the Pro models is the dedicated Telephoto lens, longer zoom range and more advanced pro photo and video controls.
The iPhone Duo also has two 48MP rear cameras, with Main and Ultra Wide lenses plus a 2x optical-quality crop from the Main sensor. Its folding design introduces some unusual camera features, including Duo Preview and Smart Take, but it lacks the dedicated Telephoto and variable-aperture Main camera found on the Pro models.
The iPhone Air and iPhone 17e are the least versatile current models, because each has only a single 48MP rear camera. Both can produce a 12MP optical-quality 2x view from the Main sensor, but neither has an Ultra Wide camera. The Air does at least get the newer 18MP Center Stage front camera, while the 17e retains a 12MP TrueDepth camera.
The older iPhone 16 sits somewhere in between, with a 48MP Main camera and 12MP Ultra Wide, plus the same 2x optical-quality crop from the Main sensor. It is still a capable camera phone, but the iPhone 17 improves the Ultra Wide to 48MP and upgrades the front camera.
Our recommendation: If photography and video are your priority, buy the iPhone 18 Pro. It gives you exactly the same camera system as the Pro Max for less money and in a more manageable size.
$1199 at  Apple						
					


						

							




iPhone camera specifications compared
Here’s how the current iPhone cameras compare. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max share the same triple-camera system, including the variable-aperture Main camera and 4x/8x Telephoto setup, while the iPhone 17 steps down to dual 48MP Main and Ultra Wide cameras. The iPhone Air and 17e are less versatile, each using a single 48MP rear camera. Most newer models also feature Apple’s 18MP Center Stage front camera with automatic reframing and Dual Capture, while the iPhone 17e retains a 12MP TrueDepth camera and the iPhone Duo uses separate outer and inner front cameras.

Which iPhone has the best battery life? 

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




The iPhone 18 Pro Max has the best battery life of any current iPhone, with Apple rating it for up to 45 hours of video playback. That puts it comfortably ahead of the rest of the lineup and makes endurance one of the biggest reasons to choose it over the smaller iPhone 18 Pro. Its longer battery life comes from a combination of a larger battery, the more efficient 2nm A20 Pro chip, and Apple’s lower-power C2 modem.
The iPhone Duo comes surprisingly close when used with its smaller 5.4-inch outer display, offering up to 44 hours of video playback. However, battery life drops to around 31 hours when using the larger 7.6-inch folding display, so the Pro Max remains the better choice if maximum endurance is your priority.
If you want strong battery life without carrying the much larger and heavier Pro Max, the iPhone 18 Pro is an excellent compromise at up to 36 hours, while the iPhone 17 remains the best mainstream option at up to 30 hours.
Our recommendation: If battery life matters above everything else, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is the clear choice. Its combination of a 45-hour rating, huge 6.9-inch display and Pro-level performance makes it particularly well suited to heavy users, travelers and anyone who wants to get through a long day without worrying about charging.

Which iPhone has the best display? 
The iPhone Duo has the biggest and most distinctive display of any current iPhone. Opened up, its 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR OLED screen offers around 50 percent more screen area than the iPhone 18 Pro Max, making it especially good for video, gaming, reading and multitasking. The inner display supports 120Hz ProMotion, Always-On and up to 3,000 nits of outdoor brightness, while a nano-texture finish helps reduce reflections and make the fold crease less noticeable. There is also a 5.4-inch outer OLED display with 120Hz ProMotion and 3,000-nit outdoor brightness.
If you want the best conventional iPhone display, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is the standout choice. Its 6.9-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display combines an adaptive 1Hz to 120Hz ProMotion refresh rate, Always-On support and up to 3,000 nits of outdoor brightness. Ceramic Shield 2 provides additional protection, while Apple has also reduced the bezels and made the Dynamic Island smaller. The iPhone 18 Pro offers essentially the same display technology at a more manageable 6.3 inches.
You no longer need to buy a Pro model to get Apple’s best core display technology, though. The iPhone 17 and iPhone Air also support ProMotion and Always-On, features that were previously reserved for Pro iPhones. Both reach 3,000 nits outdoors, with the iPhone 17 offering a 6.3-inch screen and the Air a larger 6.5-inch display. That makes the iPhone 17 particularly strong value if you want a premium screen without paying Pro prices.
The older iPhone 16 and iPhone 17e are a noticeable step down. Neither supports ProMotion or Always-On, so their displays are limited to 60Hz. The iPhone 16 reaches up to 2,000 nits outdoors, while the 17e is dimmer still, with peak HDR brightness of 1,200 nits. The 17e also lacks the newer models’ ability to dim the display all the way down to 1 nit.
Our recommendation: Ultimately, screen size may matter as much as display technology. Choose the iPhone Duo if you want the largest and most versatile screen, the iPhone 18 Pro Max for the best conventional large-screen iPhone, or the iPhone 17 if you want most of the premium display experience for considerably less money.
$1999 at  Apple						
					


						

							


Which iPhone is fastest?
The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are the fastest iPhones you can buy, thanks to Apple’s new A20 Pro chip. The processor uses a 2nm manufacturing process and combines a six-core CPU with a seven-core GPU, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine and 50 percent more memory bandwidth than the previous A19 Pro. Apple says the GPU is up to 40 percent faster, while AI processing performance is roughly doubled.
The Pro models also benefit from a much larger vapor chamber and a new chip-packaging design inspired by Apple’s M-series processors. Apple claims these changes deliver up to 40 percent better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro, which should matter most during gaming, video editing and demanding on-device AI workloads.
The iPhone Duo uses the same full A20 Pro chip, including all seven GPU cores, so peak performance should be very similar. However, its folding design makes cooling more difficult, so sustained performance is expected to be slightly lower than on the iPhone 18 Pro. Apple still claims up to 35 percent higher sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro.
Further down the lineup, the iPhone Air uses the A19 Pro but with one fewer GPU core and less thermal headroom, while the iPhone 17 uses the standard A19 and the iPhone 17e a reduced-GPU version of that chip.
Our recommendation: For most people, all of these phones are more than fast enough. But if you want the best performance for gaming, video work or intensive AI tasks, the iPhone 18 Pro or 18 Pro Max is the clear choice.


						

							


Which iPhone is best for gaming? 
The iPhone 18 Pro is the best iPhone for gaming for most people. It combines Apple’s new A20 Pro chip with a seven-core GPU, 50 percent more memory bandwidth than the A19 Pro, and a much larger vapor-chamber cooling system. Apple says the GPU is up to 40 percent faster and sustained performance is up to 40 percent better than on the iPhone 17 Pro, improvements that should matter most during long gaming sessions. Its 6.3-inch 120Hz ProMotion display also delivers smooth, responsive gameplay without making the phone especially bulky.
The iPhone 18 Pro Max offers essentially the same gaming performance, but its 6.9-inch display and much longer battery life make it the better option for gamers who prioritize screen size and endurance. Apple rates it for up to 45 hours of video playback, compared with 36 hours for the 18 Pro.
The iPhone Duo is an interesting alternative. It uses the same A20 Pro chip with a seven-core GPU and vapor-chamber cooling, while its 7.6-inch inner ProMotion display provides far more room for games. The trade-offs are its much higher price, 254g weight and folding form factor.
The iPhone Air and iPhone 17 are still very capable gaming phones, but they sit below the A20 Pro models for sustained graphics performance.
Our recommendation: For most gamers, choose the iPhone 18 Pro; choose the 18 Pro Max if you want the biggest conventional screen and longest battery life.


						

							


Which iPhone is best value
The iPhone 17 is the best-value iPhone overall because it gives you the strongest balance of price, display, cameras, storage and battery life without paying Pro prices.
For $899/£899, you get a 6.3-inch 120Hz ProMotion Always-On display, the A19 chip, dual 48MP rear cameras, an 18MP Center Stage front camera, 256GB of storage as standard and up to 30 hours of video playback. That is a substantial step up from the iPhone 17e, which is cheaper but drops ProMotion, Always-On and the Ultra Wide camera.
The iPhone 17e is still the best budget choice if keeping the purchase price down matters most. It starts lower, still has the A19 chip and 256GB of storage, and offers excellent battery life, but its simpler display and single rear camera make it less complete.
Our recommendation: Choose the iPhone 17 for the best overall value, or the iPhone 17e if your priority is spending as little as possible.
$599 at  Apple						
					


						

							




How to choose the right iPhone specs  
Choosing the right iPhone isn’t just about picking the newest model. You’ll also want to think about how much storage you need, what screen size feels comfortable, how much weight you’re willing to carry, and whether features such as ProMotion, advanced cameras, longer battery life or extra performance are worth paying for. The right balance will depend on how you use your phone: someone who mainly messages, browses and takes occasional photos will have very different needs from someone who shoots lots of video, plays demanding games or wants a large display for reading and media.







How much iPhone storage do you need?
Choosing the right amount of storage is important because you can’t add more internal storage later. iPhones don’t have a microSD card slot, so it’s worth thinking about how much space you’ll need over the lifetime of the phone before you buy.
The good news is that all of Apple’s current generation iPhones start with 256GB, including the iPhone 17e. That’s a much more comfortable starting point than 128GB, particularly as 48MP photos, 4K video, large games and system data all take up more space than they used to. It also makes the older 128GB iPhone 16 look like relatively poor value if it is only $100/£100 less than a newer model with twice the storage.
For most people, 256GB is the sweet spot. Before deciding, check how much storage you’re currently using by going to Settings > General > iPhone Storage. If you’re already close to your limit, move up a capacity when you upgrade.
Several things can quickly eat into your available space:
Photos and videos: 48MP photos and 4K video files are much larger than older formats.
Apple Intelligence: Apple’s AI features require several gigabytes of dedicated storage.
Apps and games: Some modern games can take up many gigabytes.
System data: iOS, caches and logs can consume a significant amount of space over time.
Which storage size should you buy?
128GB: Only worth considering on an older discounted model if you mostly stream content and rely heavily on cloud storage.
256GB: The best choice for most people, with enough room for apps, photos, videos and several years of use.
512GB: Ideal if you shoot lots of 4K video, keep a large offline media library or install many large games.
1TB or 2TB: Best suited to photographers, videographers and creators who regularly work with ProRAW or ProRes files.
Can you add more storage later?
No. You can’t upgrade an iPhone’s internal storage after purchase. You can, however, free up space with iCloud+, which lets you keep full-resolution photos and videos in the cloud while storing smaller optimized versions on the iPhone. You can also connect a USB-C SSD or flash drive to compatible iPhones to transfer files or, on supported Pro models, record ProRes video directly to external storage.
Our recommendation: Buy as much storage as you can comfortably afford. You can’t add more later, and paying a little extra upfront is often preferable to running out of space a few years down the line.
Read How much storage do you need on an iPhone? for more advice.


						

							


Which iPhone processor should you choose?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple’s A-series chips have consistently set the benchmark for smartphone performance, but the current lineup now spans several generations and performance tiers. At the top is the A20 Pro, which powers the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo. It is Apple’s first iPhone chip built on a 2nm process and features a six-core CPU, seven-core GPU, Dual 16-core Neural Engine and 50 percent more memory bandwidth than the A19 Pro. Apple says CPU performance is up to 20 percent faster than the A19 Pro, while GPU performance is up to 40 percent faster, with roughly double the AI compute performance.
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are the best choices if you want maximum performance, particularly for demanding games, video editing or intensive Apple Intelligence tasks. Their larger vapor chamber and revised chip packaging also improve sustained performance, with Apple claiming up to 40 percent better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro. The iPhone Duo uses the same full A20 Pro chip, including all seven GPU cores, although its folding design places greater constraints on cooling.
The previous-generation A19 Pro remains very capable. It powered the now-discontinued iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max and is still used in the iPhone Air. The Pro models used the full six-core GPU, while the Air has five GPU cores and less thermal headroom. The standard iPhone 17 uses the A19, while the iPhone 17e uses a cut-down version with a four-core GPU. Both are still more than fast enough for everyday use, multitasking, gaming and Apple Intelligence.
Our recommendation: For most people, processor choice shouldn’t be the deciding factor: even the A19 offers more performance than typical users need. Choose an A20 Pro iPhone if you want the fastest graphics, best sustained performance and strongest long-term headroom; otherwise, the A19 in the iPhone 17 offers the best balance of speed and value. for everyday use, gaming and AI features. For most buyers, the choice between models is likely to come down to cameras and other features rather than processor speed alone.


						

							


Finding the iPhone dimensions and design that suit you

				
					

				
			
Which iPhone has the best looks?

Apple




Once you’ve narrowed down the features you need, think about which iPhone will actually be comfortable to carry and use every day. Screen size is only part of the story: dimensions, weight, thickness and materials can make two similarly sized iPhones feel very different.
The most distinctive model is the iPhone Duo. Folded, it is short and wide at 117.8 x 84.1 x 11.3mm, but opens to 164.6mm wide and just 5.2mm thick, with a 7.6-inch inner display. At 254g, it is also the heaviest current iPhone. It uses a titanium frame, has Touch ID in the side button, and keeps Camera Control but drops the Action button.
At the other extreme is the iPhone Air, which is only 5.64mm thick and 165g, despite having a 6.5-inch display. Its titanium frame and single rear camera make it the obvious choice if low weight and thinness matter more than camera versatility or maximum battery life.
The iPhone 18 Pro measures 150 x 71.9 x 8.75mm and 211g, while the 18 Pro Max is 163.4 x 78 x 8.75mm and 249g. The Pro Max is substantially heavier, so it’s worth handling one before buying. The iPhone 17 sits in the middle at 149.6 x 71.5 x 7.95mm and 177g, making its 6.3-inch display easier to manage.

Design differences
Most current iPhones include Camera Control, the touch-sensitive side control for launching the Camera app and adjusting settings. The iPhone 17e is the exception. The Action button is also standard on most recent models, although the Duo omits it.
Camera layouts vary too. The 18 Pro and Pro Max have three rear cameras across a broad Camera Plateau, the Duo and iPhone 17 use dual-camera systems, and the Air and 17e have a single rear camera.
Color choices vary by model, from understated finishes on the Pro and Duo to brighter options on the iPhone 17 and iPhone 16, so your preferred look may help narrow down the choice.
Durability
The newer iPhone 18 Pro models, iPhone 17, Air and 17e use Ceramic Shield 2 on the front, while the Air and Pro models also add extra protection to the rear. Current iPhones are also rated IP68 for water and dust resistance, but that doesn’t make them waterproof, so a case is still a sensible precaution.
Our recommendation: Choose the iPhone Air if portability matters most, the iPhone 17 or 18 Pro for the best balance of size and usability, the Pro Max for a larger screen and battery, or the Duo if you specifically want the foldable design.







Best way to buy an iPhone
There are several ways to buy an iPhone, each with its own advantages. The two main options are buying directly from Apple or through a mobile carrier. In the U.S., iPhones are typically purchased on a carrier contract and are often locked to that network. In the U.K., you can also buy an unlocked, SIM-free iPhone outright from Apple or other retailers, either at full price or with a discount.
Buy directly from Apple

				
					

				
			
Jon Stoa




Pros: You can get an unlocked, SIM-free phone (in most regions), access to the iPhone Upgrade Program, and the ability to trade in your old device for credit (up to $650). It’s also the best place to pre-order a new model for the fastest delivery.
Cons: You almost always pay full retail price.
Buy from a Carrier
Pros: This is where you’ll find the biggest discounts, often in the form of bill credits over 24 or 36 months when you trade in a phone and sign up for a qualifying plan. For example, AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon frequently offer up to $830–$1,000 off new iPhones with a trade-in .
Cons: These deals come with significant strings attached, including long-term contracts and specific plan requirements. Always read the fine print
A contract usually starts with an upfront payment that will vary depending on the iPhone model you go for and also how much you’ll be paying each month. That upfront payment is followed by monthly payments, normally for a total of 24 months, after which you own the phone (in most cases). Those monthly payments also cover data, minutes and texts.
The following networks are worth checking for their contract offers:
AT&T
Sprint
T-Mobile
Verizon
Optimum Mobile
Boost Infinite
U.K. readers can find iPhone contracts from the following networks:
O2
EE
Vodafone
Three
Tesco Mobile
Sky Mobile
Virgin Mobile
Carphone Warehouse
Mobiles.co.uk
E2save
Mobile Phones Direct


						

							


Buy from a third-party reseller
Pros: In the U.K., resellers like Amazon, Currys, and John Lewis frequently sell unlocked iPhones at a discount, often offering the best upfront savings . For instance, Amazon has offered £200 off the iPhone Air.
Cons: Availability and deals change frequently.
You could try the following third-party resellers:
Amazon 
Ao.com
Argos
Currys
John Lewis
Buy via Apple’s iPhone Upgrade Program
Apple offers financing and upgrade options that let you spread the cost of an iPhone over monthly payments, although the schemes differ between the U.S. and U.K.
In the U.S., Apple has ceased the old iPhone Upgrade Program and now directs customers to Apple Upgrade, a lease-based option that lets you make monthly payments and upgrade to a new device at the end of the lease by returning your current one. Apple also offers carrier deals, financing and outright purchase options. 
In the U.K., Apple has replaced the traditional iPhone Upgrade Programme with a Flexible Finance Account with Upgrade Option, provided by Creation. Eligible iPhones can be bought on a 20-month 0% plan with an upgrade option after 11 payments, or a 30-month 0% plan with an upgrade option after 23 payments. Current plans start from £64.95 a month for the 20-month option or £43.30 a month for the 30-month option. 
Whether these plans are good value depends on how often you upgrade. They can be convenient if you like replacing your iPhone regularly, but if you usually keep a phone for several years, buying outright or using standard 0% finance may work out cheaper overall.


						

							


Buy a refurbished iPhone

				
					

				
			
Apple




Buying an iPhone doesn’t come cheap. However, if you’re strapped for cash you don’t have to dismiss the idea of buying an iPhone completely. You may be able to get a good deal on a refurbished model. 
Buying a refurbished iPhone is a smart way to save money while still getting a premium device, but the key is knowing where to shop and what to look for.
Understand the difference between refurbished vs used
Refurbished: Professionally inspected, tested and repaired where necessary. It should come with a warranty and may also have a replacement battery.
Used or second-hand: Usually sold by an individual in its current condition, often without a warranty or any guarantee that it is fully functional. There is also a greater risk of hidden faults or Activation Lock problems.
What to check before buying
Warranty: Choose a seller offering a meaningful warranty, ideally for at least 12 months.
Condition grade: Sellers use grades such as A, B and C, or Fair, Good and Excellent. Higher grades indicate less cosmetic wear but usually cost more.
Battery health: Check the seller’s minimum battery-capacity guarantee. Many refurbished sellers promise at least 80% of the battery’s original capacity, while Apple-furbished iPhones receive a new battery.
Unlocked or locked: Confirm that the iPhone is unlocked and can be used with your preferred mobile network. This is particularly important when buying in the U.S.
Model age: Avoid iPhones that are close to losing software support. As of mid-2026, the iPhone XS, XS Max and XR are no longer sensible long-term purchases, while the iPhone 11 should be approached with caution.
Shop at Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store
Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store is generally the safest place to start and sets the standard for refurbished quality.
Apple thoroughly tests each device, replaces the battery and outer shell, and supplies it in a new box with the appropriate accessories. Refurbished iPhones also come with Apple’s standard one-year warranty, 90 days of technical support and the option to add AppleCare+.
Prices are typically around 15% lower than the original retail price, although availability varies. Apple operates refurbished stores in both the U.S. and U.K.
Consider other trusted resellers
If you can’t find what you need at Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store, try one of these places to buy a refurbished iPhone.
U.S.:
Back Market: You get 30 days to change your mind and a 12-month warranty… or occasionally more. Take careful note of the phone’s quality rating as the cheapest will have more visible signs of wear (stratches and scuffs) than the more expensive Excellent and Premium buys. Premium-quality iPhones also have the highest-rated batteries and only Apple parts.
Amazon Renewed Store: This site’s greatest benefit is that purchases are all backed by Amazon’s standard returns policy and its “Renewed Guarantee” lets you get a refund or replacement within a year of receiving your product.
Best Buy: Best Buy doesn’t offer a great deal of information on pre-owned iPhones’ condition, but you can return within 14 days if the item is “unopened or defective in any way.”
Walmart: Walmart doesn’t sell refurbished iPhones directly; rather, they are sourced from other sellers. Return policies vary from seller to seller, but there are minimum requirements that apply universally.
U.K.: 
Back Market: You get 30 days to change your mind and a 12-month warranty… or occasionally more. See above for more details on Back Market’s quality rankings.
Music Magpie: A good place to start looking for refurbished iPhones with a one-year warranty. You may find that sales reduce the price still further.
Hoxton Macs: Don’t let the Mac in the name fool you. Hoxton Macs has started selling refurbished iPhones, with a one-year Return to Base warranty.
Reboxed: Pledges that devices “are fully tested and in perfect working order.” All come with a 12-month no quibble warranty.
Amazon Renewed Store: While you can’t really sell on Amazon Renewed unless you’re a business, those looking to buy a refurbished iPhone Amazon Renewed have plenty of options to choose from. Its greatest benefit is that purchases are all backed by Amazon’s standard returns policy and its “Renewed Guarantee” lets you get a refund or replacement within 1 year of receiving your product.
Envirofone: Also allows you to trade in your old phone for credit towards purchasing a refurbished phone.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Unboxing: New Colors, Better Photos, and Smaller Dynamic Island
content:
The iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max are launching tomorrow, but we were able to get one early to share some initial impressions.

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.

Both the 18 Pro and Pro Max are heavier than the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max models they replace, and it's most noticeable when you pick up the Pro Max. It was a heavy phone to begin with, and now there's more weight (249 grams vs. 233 grams).

If you hated last year's two-tone design with the contrast between the aluminum frame and the glass back, there's good news. Apple is now matching the glass to the frame for a more uniform look.

Our review unit is Apple's new glacier color, which is a light blue that's slightly different from the other light blue shades Apple has used in the past. Unlike some of those blues, the glacier color actually looks blue and not silver. Apple is also offering the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models in burgundy, silver, and black. We have a burgundy model on the way and will share that in the future.

There's a fancy new 2nm A20 Pro chip inside the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and Pro Max, but depending on what you're upgrading from, you might not notice much in the way of performance. iPhones have used wildly fast chips for the last several years, and you're not stressing the processor when browsing the web and scrolling social media sites. What you might notice is the new vapor chamber cooling system. It takes up three times more surface area, so the iPhone stays cooler when you are doing something that takes a little more processing power like playing a game. Battery life has improved, but that's not something we've had time to test yet. Apple says you'll get up to 36 hours of video playback with the 18 Pro and 45 hours with the 18 Pro Max.

If you're in the U.S. and buying an ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌, it will have Apple's new C2 modem, but if you get the 18 Pro Max, it's going to have a Qualcomm modem. Both models use the C2 outside of the U.S. The C2 modem has mmWave 5G for the first time, plus it's more efficient than Qualcomm modems, so it will be interesting to see some speed tests comparing the two.

Dynamic Island by putting the infrared camera under the display, and that's the most noticeable change on the front of the device. It takes up less space, and Apple also updated it so it can show three Live Activities at once or two in more detail.

There's a new variable aperture Main camera that also has a new sensor, plus Apple tweaked its computational imaging pipeline. With a variable aperture lens, there's more control over lighting and depth of field. If it's super bright outside, the iPhone can automatically adjust the aperture to let in less light. If it's dark, a wider aperture will let in more light. There are four aperture settings in total, and it works behind the scenes so you can just snap photos as usual. You'll probably notice it most in low lighting.

If you want to control the aperture yourself, you can do so with new Pro Controls that also give you the option to adjust shutter speed and white balance. There's a histogram too so you can check exposure levels.

We'll have a full video on the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ camera system coming next week.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Launching Tomorrow With These 10 New Features
content:
Apple last week unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. While the devices look very similar to the iPhone 17 Pro models, there are still quite a few new features and incremental changes compared to the previous generation.


Below, we have recapped 10 new features coming with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have been available to pre-order since Saturday, September 12 and will begin arriving to customers and launch in stores this Friday, September 18.

A20 Pro chip, the first 2nm chip in an iPhone. It has a 6-core CPU, a 7-core GPU, and a 32-core Neural Engine. Apple says the chip delivers up to 20% faster CPU performance and up to 40% faster graphics performance compared to the A19 Pro chip in the iPhone 17 Pro. Apple also says sustained performance is up to 40% faster.


Three new color options: Burgundy, Black, and Glacier. Orange is no longer an option. The rear aluminum and Ceramic Shield glass area are now more color matched.


A smaller Dynamic Island with support for up to three Live Activities at once.


The main 48-megapixel Fusion camera on both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max has variable aperture, allowing you to adjust the amount of light that reaches the image sensor for greater control over depth of field. Apple says this upgrade will allow for improved low-light photography and crisper details in the back of group photos. Aperture options include ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, and ƒ/4.0.


In the Camera app on iPhone 18 Pro models, new Pro controls allow you to manually control or adjust shutter speed, white balance, and aperture, and there is an option to use a histogram.


iPhone 18 Pro models can record time-lapse videos in 4K and Dolby Vision HDR.


Both of the iPhone 18 Pro models have longer battery life compared to the previous generation — especially the iPhone 18 Pro Max. If we go by Apple's offline video playback metric, the iPhone 18 Pro Max has up to 15% longer battery life compared to the iPhone 17 Pro Max. Fast charging to 50% now takes 15 minutes, down from 20 minutes.


The revamped vapor chamber cooling system in the iPhone 18 Pro models has three times more surface area than the one in the iPhone 17 Pro models, for even better heat dissipation.


iPhone 18 Pro models worldwide are equipped with Apple's second-generation C2 cellular modem for 5G and LTE, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max has it in every country except for the U.S., where it has a Qualcomm modem. Apple says the C2 chip has "AI-powered improvements" to cellular quality and reliability, delivering "meaningfully faster uploads when compared to its previous C1X modem while consuming 15% less energy. In the U.S., the chip supports mmWave 5G.


There is now a 2TB storage capacity for both the Pro and Pro Max models — it was previously exclusive to the iPhone 17 Pro Max.

title: First glimpses of Siri AI in French, Spanish, and other new languages appear
content:
Macworld





Siri AI has arrived, and the general public can finally join the waiting list and enjoy the upgraded voice assistant’s improved features and accuracy. Provided their device is set to English, that is.
When Siri AI was first announced, Apple explained that it would initially be available in English only, but the latest beta has indicated that a batch of further languages will be added next month. Specifically, speakers of French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish will get access to Siri AI in October.
Such promises don’t always come true, but we’ve already had our first glimpse of the new languages. As spotted by MacRumors, they’re present in the iOS 27.2 beta, well in advance of the self-imposed deadline.
There’s no hard and fast rule covering the time it takes an iOS update to move from beta to public release, but it shouldn’t be too much of a challenge for Apple to roll out iOS 27.2 within the next 44 days. So the inclusion of the new languages offers a clue about when the update will appear. The iPhone Duo, which will be running iOS 27.1 at launch, launches on October 23, another possible clue to the timing.
Apple hasn’t offered any comment on when further languages will be added to Siri AI. But it’s likely that Mandarin and Cantonese aren’t a high priority at the moment, because Siri AI isn’t launching in mainland China, at least for the time being, for legal/regulatory reasons.

title: iPhone 15 Pro vs. iPhone 18 Pro Buyer's Guide: Should You Upgrade?
content:
Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max earlier this month, arriving three years after the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max. Three generations of changes make for a substantial upgrade, bringing larger displays, an all-new design, improvements to every camera, significantly longer battery life, and faster charging.


The iPhone 16 Pro introduced larger displays with thinner borders, the Camera Control, a 48-megapixel Ultra Wide camera, and improved video and audio recording. The iPhone 17 Pro replaced the titanium frame and glass back with an aluminum unibody, added vapor chamber cooling and Ceramic Shield 2, and upgraded both the telephoto and front-facing cameras. This year's refresh centers on the A20 Pro chip, a variable-aperture Main camera, a smaller Dynamic Island, and a further increase in battery capacity. For iPhone 15 Pro owners, all three sets of changes accumulate.

starts at $1,199 for 256GB, $200 more than the iPhone 15 Pro's $999 launch price, although the entry storage tier has doubled from 128GB. The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max starts at $1,299, $100 more than the iPhone 15 Pro Max's equivalent starting configuration. Here are the key differences between the iPhone 15 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌:

Design and Display








iPhone 15 Pro (2023)
‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ (2026)


Brushed titanium frame with full glass back
Aluminum unibody with partial Ceramic Shield back, improving heat dissipation


Glass rounded square camera bump
Full-width rounded rectangle aluminum camera plateau


iPhone 15 Pro: 6.1-inch display

Which to Choose?

For iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max owners considering a replacement, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ is a worthwhile upgrade. Three generations of changes bring improvements to the display, each camera on the device, battery life, charging, and sustained performance. Battery life is likely to be the strongest argument for most users, particularly if their current device no longer comfortably lasts through the day, while faster wired charging makes brief charging stops more useful. 

The camera upgrade is especially compelling for anyone who regularly takes photos or records video. Higher-resolution Ultra Wide and Telephoto cameras expand the options beyond the Main camera, while the variable aperture and Pro controls provide additional creative flexibility. The Camera Control also offers a dedicated way to launch the camera and adjust settings, although its value will depend on whether you prefer physical controls to the touchscreen.

Owners of the smaller iPhone 15 Pro gain more native telephoto reach, moving from 3x to 4x, as well as the optical-quality 8x option. For iPhone 15 Pro Max owners, the camera moves from 5x to 4x, with the higher-resolution sensor enabling the additional 8x crop. 

For video creators, the accumulated changes are more consequential still. Higher-frame-rate 4K recording, ProRes RAW, Genlock, Apple Log 2, Dual Capture, and improved audio tools expand the range of work that can be completed on the device. The square front-camera sensor also makes landscape framing easier without rotating the phone, while Center Stage improves flexibility for group photos and video calls.

iOS 27, Apple Intelligence, or ‌Visual Intelligence‌ alone does not require replacing it.

There are physical trade-offs to consider. Both newer models are larger and thicker, with weight increasing by 24 grams on the Pro and 28 grams on the Pro Max. The aluminum enclosure improves heat flow, but it may show dents and scratches more readily than the titanium frame. Users who chose the iPhone 15 Pro for its relatively compact size and light weight may find those changes less appealing, even with the improvements in screen size and battery life.

Siri AI. A battery replacement may be worth considering if reduced health is your main complaint and you would otherwise be happy to keep the device. The upgrade becomes much easier to recommend when battery limitations coincide with a desire for the newer cameras, larger display, or improved performance.

A discounted ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ is another option if your priorities are the aluminum design, higher-resolution telephoto camera, square front-camera sensor, and vapor chamber cooling. Those upgrades arrived before this year's model. Paying more for the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ makes the clearest sense when you also want the variable aperture, Pro controls, A20 Pro, smaller ‌Dynamic Island‌, and further improvements to battery life and charging.

title: 50 New macOS Golden Gate Features and Changes Worth Checking Out
content:
Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate this week, and despite the company's focus this year on refining its flagship operating system, improving performance, and nixing bugs, there are still plenty of new things to explore. There's an overhauled Siri experience, changes across Apple's apps, and much-needed updates across the system interface. 



In this article, we've selected 50 new features and lesser-known changes that are worth checking out if you're updating your Mac. Siri AI remains in beta and is initially rolling out in English, and the availability of some features varies by language and region. What do you think of ‌macOS Golden Gate so far? Let us know in the comments.

Siri AI Replaces the Old Siri Experience

 
In macOS 27, Apple has turned Spotlight into the place to search your Mac or ask Siri AI a question. From the new "Search or Ask" bar, you can hold a conversation with Siri, find relevant information in apps such as Mail and Photos, and take actions in supported apps. 

Adjustable Liquid Glass Transparency Slider

 
System Settings now has a slider that lets users adjust Liquid Glass from ultra-clear to fully tinted (found in Appearance ➝ Liquid Glass). Apple has also improved contrast and window shadows, standardized macOS toolbars, and made sidebars extend to the edges of app windows. The changes aim to make controls easier to read and active windows easier to distinguish.

Safari's Start Page Can Resume a Browsing Topic

 
Safari's Start Page has a new Recently Viewed section that brings back your recently closed browsing topics as well as topics open on any of your other devices. It offers a handy way to pick up a search or research session without trawling through your browser history.

Visual Intelligence Comes to the Mac


Visual Intelligence is now available on the Mac. Simply press Shift-Command-Space to select something onscreen, then ask Siri to explain it, translate text, search for similar images, or find related information. Siri can also use what it recognizes to take an action, such as adding the details from an event flyer to your Calendar.

Photos Can Save a Video Frame as a Still Photo


The Photos app can now save a frame from a video as a separate photo. Pause a clip at the moment you want, right-click (or Control-click) it, then choose "Save Video Frame as Photo," and it will add the still image to your library without exporting the entire video. 

Past Conversations Are Saved in a New Siri App


macOS now has a dedicated Siri app where you can start new conversations or revisit past chats you've had with Siri. The app has a card-style interface with details on your most recent chats across all of your devices. You can also use the search button to find conversations, and there's a pin option for ones you revisit frequently. The Siri app is cross-platform and your content syncs across all of your Apple devices.

Shared Albums Go Full Resolution


Previously in Photos, pictures in a Shared Album were automatically reduced to 2,048 pixels on the long edge (except for panoramic photos, which can be up to 5,400 pixels wide). In macOS 27 though, Shared Albums finally support full-resolution photos and videos. But there comes a major trade-off. For years now, Apple has allowed you to store up to 5,000 photos and videos in Shared Albums without impacting your iCloud storage limit. That's no longer the case in Golden Gate.

Non-Apple Users Can Add to Shared Albums


People using Android or Windows can now join and contribute to your Shared Albums through iCloud.com. Users can also set an album to expire after 30 days, filter its photos and videos, review recent activity, and react to images with any emoji. Just remember that if you share an album with someone, what they add to it counts against your iCloud storage limit.

Photos Can Reframe Images


Photos has a new advanced editing tool in macOS 27. Reframe uses information captured with a compatible photo to change its apparent camera angle. It works by combining AI and spatial images so you can change the perspective or composition of a picture.

Photos Can Extend Images


Photos has another new editing feature: Extend lets you change the crop of an image, expanding the borders around content to zoom out a bit or change the photo's composition. It uses generative AI to fill in missing areas, and you can adjust the borders with drag gestures.

Cleaning Up Photos Got a Lot Better
 

Clean Up now uses new AI models, and it's better at removing objects. The original version of Clean Up was best for small items with little complexity in the surrounding area, but now it can do more work reconstructing backgrounds with generative AI. It also offers Fast, High Quality, and Auto modes. Apple says usage limits may apply.

Swipe Down to Refresh Comes to Mac Apps

 
The familiar swipe-down-to-refresh gesture comes to Safari, Mail, News, Podcasts, and Calendar on the Mac. Pulling down on content via your trackpad (or with your finger on iPad via Sidecar) causes the app to load the latest information, meaning you don't have to reach for a refresh button or keyboard shortcut.

Mail Search Puts More Relevant Results First


In Mail, search actually works properly in macOS 27. It now ranks messages by relevance rather than relying on matching words and recency. A search for a store, for example, can put an order confirmation ahead of promotional emails from the same sender, even if the order is buried in the inbox.

App Icons Gain More Liquid Glass Detail


Apple's app icons now have more layers of Liquid Glass, which adds detail and sharper edges across light, dark, clear, and tinted appearances. It's a smaller visual change than the new Appearance slider, but one you'll see throughout the Dock and app grid.

iPhone Mirroring Windows Become Resizable


Users can now drag a corner of an iPhone Mirroring window to make it larger or wider. Supported apps can show more information as the window expands, and macOS 27 now also supports playback of protected video in the mirrored window. Bear in mind that individual streaming providers may still restrict what can be mirrored, and iPhone Mirroring remains unavailable in the European Union.

Write With Siri Almost Anywhere


Write with Siri can generate a draft from a description, give feedback on existing text, or make a requested edit, such as shortening a paragraph or changing its tone. It works virtually anywhere you can type, and Apple says it can match your writing style in Mail and Messages.

Photos Adds Keywords and Star Ratings


Photos now lets users add keywords and one-to-five-star ratings to both photos and videos. Ratings can also be used as a filter, so it's easier to narrow down a large library to your best shots. Ratings controls are off by default, but you can enable them in Photos' General settings by checking the box next to "Show Rating Controls."

Add Extra-Large Widgets to Desktop


If you have any widgets on your desktop, try right-clicking (or Ctrl-clicking) on them and looking for a new option called Extra-Large Portrait. You can now make widgets take up a lot more screen space, which is useful for things like weather, home, and reminder widgets.

Trade in Siri for ChatGPT


The new Siri app and the "Search or Ask" bar (Command-Space) defaults to the new Siri AI, but you can switch it to ChatGPT if you prefer. Simply right-click (or Ctrl-click) and select "Ask..." From the context menu, and you'll see an option to change to ChatGPT. Note that conversation context doesn't transfer when you switch chatbot providers.

Safari Organizes Pages for You


If you have several webpages open with related content, Safari can automatically group these open tabs by topic while keeping any unrelated browsing sessions apart. To enable the feature, open Safari's Settings, select the Tabs section, and choose "Organize Tabs: Automatically Create Topics."

Safari Can Notify You When a Page Changes


Notify Me is another new Safari feature that enables the browser to watch a webpage for a specific change, such as a product restock or price drop, and alert you when it happens. The feature's monitoring options include daily, weekly, or monthly schedules.

Apple Notes Now Lets You Draw


The Continuity feature has allowed you to sketch in the Notes app by opening a virtual drawing board on your iPhone or iPad. But that meant you had to have at least one iOS device linked to your Apple Account. Happily, that's no longer a requirement in macOS 27, which adds a native drawing tool to the Notes app. It includes Pen, Monoline, Marker, Pencil, Crayon, Fountain Pen, Reed, and Watercolor tools.

Video Podcasts Get Better Mac Playback

 
The Podcasts app gives video shows fuller playback controls on the Mac, including Picture in Picture and a download option for offline viewing. You can switch between watching and listening when a show supports video, and the search function in a show's episode list makes older episodes easier to find.

Image Playground Gets More Styles


Image Playground has been overhauled to become genuinely useful, and it can now generate pictures in a wider range of styles, including photorealistic images. You can select part of an image and describe how you want it changed, or combine images to create something new. As with other Apple Intelligence features, Apple says usage limits may apply.

New Golden Gate Wallpapers Arrive


Golden Gate includes Sunset and Night wallpapers featuring San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge, along with a new abstract wallpaper. The Bridge wallpapers animate when your Mac unlocks and you can also use them as your screen savers.

Safari Can Build Extensions From a Description


Safari's Create an Extension option lets you describe what you want a browser extension to do in plain language. For example, a request to add a button for saving recipes can become a custom extension without you having to go near a single line of code. Safari also offers suggested prompts for productivity, focus, and design tasks.

Freeform Adds Drawing, Collaborative Folders


Freeform now supports drawing directly on the Mac, thanks to sketching tools being included in its shared boards. Golden Gate also adds folders for organizing collaborative boards and a canvas that adapts to Dark Mode.

Faster AirDrop and Network Browsing


Apple says Golden Gate makes AirDrop transfers and browsing folders on Windows or NAS network shares faster. Safari's Start Page content also loads more quickly, and Mission Control and Spaces animations are smoother.

Calendar Events Can Be Added by Description


Calendar can now create or edit an event from your plain-language description. You can describe a lunch meeting, change the time and adjust the description to make it a coffee meeting, and Calendar will adjust the event rather than requiring every detail to be edited separately.

Enhanced Maps Flyover


With Flyover, cities like Boston, New York, London, and Chicago include more detailed 3D renderings of their skylines. Apple has enhanced the 3D models for these cities by combining AI and aerial imagery to achieve more detailed and realistic cityscapes.

Slideshows Can Start From Any Photos Album


Photos can now create slideshows from any album or collection, rather than limiting them to Memories. You can customize the presentation and save it as a video to keep or share.

Passwords Will (Soon) Auto-Repair Weak Logins


The Passwords app already warns users about weak or compromised logins. Apple says a future software update will let it use Safari to change eligible passwords automatically, replacing a vulnerable login with a stronger one on your behalf.

External Displays Get Better Resolution Support


Golden Gate adds more resolution and refresh-rate choices for compatible external displays, including 5K at 120Hz on certain ultrawide screens. Apple also says the Mac does a better job of restoring window positions, Spaces, and screen assignments when a display is unplugged and reconnected.

macOS Suggests Names for Files and Folders


In Finder, TextEdit, and other Apple apps, Apple Intelligence can suggest a name for a file or folder based on its contents. The feature is designed to make saved items easier to recognize later, especially when the original name doesn't give much away about what's inside.

Siri Gains New Expressive Voices


Siri‌ AI now has more expressive voices alongside a big improvement to systemwide dictation accuracy. You can adjust both the expressiveness and pace of ‌Siri‌'s voice to your preference with sliders in a new Voice section in System Settings ➝ Siri. Siri's new expressive voices require an M3 or newer Mac with at least 12GB of memory.

Weather's Forecast Views Are Refreshed


Weather in macOS 27 has a more orderly layout, with more room for its hourly and 10-day forecasts. You can also switch between current conditions, precipitation, and wind views, while a new Highlights section calls out notable weather events ahead. Highlights are currently only available in U.S. English.

Create Shortcuts With Natural Language


True to this era of AI, Shortcuts can now build you an automation from a plain-language description. You can ask it to assemble a sequence of actions across apps, then test, edit, or refine the result with another description. Apple says usage limits may apply.

Finder Columns Are Easier to Size and Reset


New autosize and reset controls make columns easier to manage in Finder. Right-click (or Control-click) the bottom of a column, and you'll see options to adjust a crowded view without dragging each column boundary into place by hand.

Sidecar Finally Supports Direct Finger Input


Sidecar now lets you interact directly with the Mac interface on an iPad used as a second display. With a compatible iPad, you can tap controls, scroll with a finger, and use more system gestures instead of relying on your mouse or trackpad.

New Screen Time Controls for Parents


Parents can now set category-level allowances with different schedules by day and time, making controls more flexible than one broad daily limit. Meanwhile, Ask to Browse lets kids ask your permission to visit websites. There are also expanded protections against gore and violence, alongside existing nudity protections.

Make Interface Boundaries Clearer


A new Show Borders accessibility option makes the boundaries of macOS interface elements easier to see, in case you could do with some help distinguishing controls and panels where translucent surfaces otherwise blend into the surrounding window.

Widgets Can Update in Real Time


Widgets will now update in real time when their associated app is open, so the information you see on the desktop remains in step with what you see inside the app, instead of you having to wait for a less frequent refresh.

Dock Shows Active Background Processes


If you quit an app and it is still running a background process, you'll see the indicator beneath its Dock icon turn a light gray. To end the activity, right-click the app's icon and select "Stop Running in Background."

Photos Gains New Utility Collections

 
The Photos app now has two Utility collections. "Captured by Me" gathers pictures taken with your current and any previous iPhones, while "Identity Documents" brings together images of passports, driver's licenses, and any similar records you might have.

Intel Macs Miss Golden Gate


If you have a very old machine, there's something you should know: Golden Gate does not run on Intel Macs – it requires Apple silicon (that includes the A-series chip in MacBook Neo). Sorry, Intel users.

Rosetta Support Is Ending


macOS 27 is also the final major release with general-purpose Rosetta support for Intel-only apps on Macs with Apple silicon. Apple says those apps will stop working in the next major release, apart from certain older games.

Smart Replies Can Sound More Like You


Mail's Smart Replies are able to reflect your usual writing style when they suggest a response, right down to your tone and phrasing, so now a quick reply can sound more like something you would have written yourself. To use a smart reply, click the reply button on an email, click inside the message field, then choose one of the suggested replies generated by Apple Intelligence.

Get Context on a Phone Call


Just like in iOS 27, the Phone app on Mac supports a new Call Context feature. It can surface relevant information from the Mail app. If you call an airline, it might show your confirmation code for an upcoming flight, or your reservation code if you're calling a hotel. It doesn't listen to what you're saying, but instead looks at the number you're calling and links it to details in the Mail app.

Shortcuts Adds Screenshot and Alert Triggers


Shortcuts automations can now be triggered simply by taking a screenshot or receiving a notification. The new options add to existing triggers such as time of day, location, and app activity, giving you more ways to start a routine automatically.

Reminders Understands Natural Language

Apple said the new iPhone 18 Pro models are capable of faster USB-C charging compared to the iPhone 17 Pro models, and a new video shared by the YouTube channel Xiaobai's Tech Reviews offers a closer look at the year-over-year improvement.


As spotted by the account Ice Universe, the video reveals that the iPhone 18 Pro Max can go from 0% to 100% battery life in as little as 55 minutes with a capable charger, compared to 81 minutes for the iPhone 17 Pro Max. In other words, the iPhone 18 Pro Max can be "fully" charged 26 minutes faster compared to the previous generation (iPhones continue to receive a slow trickle of power even after they show 100% battery life).

In line with Apple's advertised claim, the video showed that the iPhone 18 Pro Max can reach 50% battery life in just 15 minutes, down from 20 minutes for the iPhone 17 Pro models.

The smaller iPhone 18 Pro should have similar charging speeds.

achieved a peak charging speed of 36W in a separate test conducted by ChargerLAB. As always, charging slows down later in a session to prevent overheating.

Exactly how useful these improvements are to you will depend on your charging habits. If you mostly charge your iPhone overnight, then faster charging is obviously not very beneficial. But if you find yourself topping up your iPhone throughout the day, then saving nearly a half hour on a 0% to 100% charge may be meaningful to you.

The video referenced is in Chinese.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 Reviews: Look Out, Oura Ring
content:
The first reviews of the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are now available ahead of the devices launching this Friday, September 18.


While both new Apple Watches look virtually identical to the previous-generation models on the outside, there are a handful of upgrades this year. For example, a more powerful S11 chip and larger LEDs on the optical heart sensor enable more accurate and frequent heart rate sensing, and HRV is now measured up to 24 times more often.

There is also a new Readiness app, more accurate step tracking, and faster charging. Finally, two new Audio Intelligence features Siri Rewind and Live Recap will be available later this year, as part of an upcoming watchOS update.

The Verge's Victoria Song said the S11 chip speeds up Siri AI:
The S11's impact was also noticeable in testing. Siri AI queries are faster on the Series 12 than my Ultra 3.
Song added that the higher-frequency heart rate sensing did not impact battery life:
I didn't notice a negative impact to battery life from continuous heart rate tracking. People will gripe that the Series 12 doesn't have multi-day battery and sticks to the Series 11's 24-hour battery estimate. But like last year, I maintain that faster charging is a fine enough solution. In a 20-minute charging test, I went from 20 to 64 percent battery.
9to5Mac's Chance Miller on Apple Watch Ultra 4 battery life:
In my testing, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 lives up to Apple's battery life claims. In my real-world test, I charged it to 100% around 8 p.m. on Sunday and didn't put it back on the charger until 8 p.m. on Tuesday. That's 48 hours on a single charge, including 90 minutes of workout tracking, three hours away from my iPhone, and two nights of sleep tracking.
CNET's Vanessa Hand Orellana noted that the Apple Watch's belated ability to show a readiness score stands apart from competitors like the Oura Ring by continuously updating throughout the day and not requiring a monthly subscription fee for some stats:
Many wearables give you a score in the morning based on metrics such as HRV, sleep, temperature and other overnight vitals, but since it's static and delivered once a day, it can feel like a life sentence (and sometimes a self-fulfilling prophecy) rather than a training tool. The Apple Watch keeps measuring your daytime vitals and adjusts your Readiness score as the day unfolds and rates you from 0–10 with actionable advice including Recover, Pace Yourself, Ready and Go for It. In theory, you could see how a midmorning nap affects your score and adjust your workout accordingly. 



Apple's readiness score requires "at least" seven nights of data, and most reviewers said they were still not seeing a score yet after around a week, so we will need to wait for later reviews to get a better look at the feature.

Siri Rewind and Live Recap were not available to reviewers yet, either, unfortunately.

Engadget's Cherlynn Low said the new models are a "solid upgrade" this year:
If you can ignore the Live Rewind and Siri Recap features that aren't even available on the Apple Watch Series 12 yet, the device is a solid upgrade over older models. The new health sensing system is a meaningful overhaul, while the expansion of gesture support has the potential to enable more hands-free interactions with your watch. The inclusion of a new type of HRV measurement, increased sampling rates and some additional watch face complications are small but helpful touches for those who obsess over their metrics.
There are some new case options and colors for the Series 12, such as Light Bronze aluminum and the return of ceramic in Pearl White and Night Blue.

title: How to downgrade iOS 27 to iOS 26 on your iPhone
content:
Macworld





Apple updates iOS every year, bestowing upon our iPhones a range of new features and security improvements, as well as the occasional redesign. In September 2026, iOS 27 made its debut. Most iPhone users will move to the new platform straight away, and the majority are likely to love the changes. But what if you encounter bugs, poor battery life, or another problem that makes you wish you could return to iOS 26?
And what if subsequent iOS 27 updates may also introduce problems that leave you wishing you could return to an earlier version?
Downgrading from iOS 27 may be possible, but only while Apple continues to sign a compatible version of iOS 26—or an earlier release of iOS 27—for your particular iPhone. There is usually only a short window in which this can be done.
In this article, we explore your options for downgrading iOS on an iPhone. Be aware that the process has significant disadvantages: it erases the device, and a backup made after installing iOS 27 generally cannot be restored to an iPhone running iOS 26.
